| E-2026-08-18-01 | 2026-08-18 | **Directive 2014/53/EU** of the European Parliament and of the Council of **16 April 2014** on the harmonisation of the laws of the Member States relating to the making available on the market of **radio equipment**, repealing Directive 1999/5/EC — the **Radio Equipment Directive (RED)**. Full OJ text, **OJ L 153/62, 22.5.2014**, 45 pp, read in full (CELEX 32014L0053) | Primary EU law | EUR-Lex official PDF, supplied locally after `eur-lex.europa.eu` was confirmed egress-blocked (HTTP 403, default deny) on 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-18 | **A** | **R14/ADR-012** (primary) · **R7** · **R8/PR13** · **ADR-011** · ADR-001 (item 8) | **revise** | **TIER A — the Official Journal text of a directive in force. Nothing outranks it in this register.** **CLOSES THE FIRST HALF OF THE RED GAP CARRIED SINCE E-2026-08-15-29** (four secondary pointers — tmc `-29`, EPSF `-35`, Secura `-52`, ERJU System Pillar `-53` — and zero primary rows). **(a) ⚠️ THE HEADLINE — RAIL HAS NO SECTORAL EXEMPTION, AND THE OTHER TWO SAFETY-CRITICAL TRANSPORT MODES DO.** **Annex I ("Equipment not covered by this Directive") lists exactly four categories: 1. radio amateurs; 2. marine equipment (Dir 96/98/EC); 3. airborne products, parts and appliances (Art 3 of Reg (EC) 216/2008); 4. custom-built evaluation kits for professionals at R&D facilities. RAIL IS NOT LISTED.** Marine got a carve-out. Aviation got a carve-out. **Rail did not.** The only other exclusion, **Art 1(3)**, covers radio equipment *exclusively* used for **public security, defence, State security and State activity in criminal law** — checked and **not applicable** to rail operational communications, whatever the ownership of the operator. **(b) FRMCS EQUIPMENT PLAINLY MEETS THE DEFINITION.** Art 2(1)(1): *radio equipment* = an electrical or electronic product which **intentionally emits and/or receives radio waves for the purpose of radio communication or radiodetermination**, or which must be completed with an accessory such as an antenna to do so. **Cab radios, on-board 5G modems/TOBA radio units and trackside gNodeB radio all fall squarely inside it.** Art 1(1) binds both *making available on the market* **and putting into service**. **CONCLUSION ON QUESTION 1 OF ADR-012 ACTION 7: YES — THE RED REACHES FRMCS RADIO EQUIPMENT. That is now settled on primary law, not inference.** **(c) BUT THE STRUCTURE IS TWO-TIER, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS ARCHITECTURALLY.** **Art 3(1) and 3(2) apply UNCONDITIONALLY to all radio equipment in scope:** 3(1)(a) protection of health and safety of persons and property **including the Directive 2014/35/EU (LVD) safety objectives "but with no voltage limit applying"**; 3(1)(b) adequate electromagnetic compatibility per Dir 2014/30/EU; 3(2) effective and efficient use of radio spectrum to avoid harmful interference. Art 1(4) confirms RED equipment is **not** subject to the LVD except through Art 3(1)(a). **Art 3(3)(a)–(i) apply ONLY to "radio equipment within certain categories or classes"** — and the closing subparagraph is the operative mechanism: *"The Commission shall be empowered to adopt **delegated acts in accordance with Article 44** specifying **which categories or classes of radio equipment are concerned by each of the requirements** set out in points (a) to (i)."* **So the cybersecurity-relevant requirements are DORMANT IN THE DIRECTIVE ITSELF AND ARE SWITCHED ON PER CLASS BY DELEGATED ACT.** The three usually described as the RED's cyber requirements are **(d) the equipment does not harm the network or its functioning nor misuse network resources, thereby causing an unacceptable degradation of service; (e) it incorporates safeguards to ensure the personal data and privacy of the user and subscriber are protected; (f) it supports certain features ensuring protection from fraud.** **(d) THE SLEEPER — Art 3(3)(i) AND Art 4 ARE A DIRECT HIT ON ADR-012'S CENTRAL TENSION, AND NOBODY IN THE SECONDARY SOURCES MENTIONED THEM.** **Art 3(3)(i): "radio equipment supports certain features in order to ensure that software can only be loaded into the radio equipment where the compliance of the COMBINATION of the radio equipment and software has been demonstrated."** And **Art 4(1)**: manufacturers of radio equipment *and of software allowing the equipment to be used as intended* must supply Member States and the Commission with information on the compliance of **intended combinations**, resulting from an Art 17 conformity assessment, as a statement of compliance per Annex VI, **"continuously updated"** — itself delegated-act-gated by Art 4(2). **ADR-012's load-bearing trade is "CRA mandates security updates over a support period; railway authorisation demands stability." If Art 3(3)(i)/Art 4 are activated for this equipment class, patching a cab radio becomes a FOUR-WAY constraint: the CRA update duty · the RED combination-compliance demonstration · a continuously-updated statement of compliance · and railway change-control/Zulassung. ADR-012 currently models two of the four.** Flagged **conditional** — both are delegated-act-gated and activation is unverified. **(e) WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLOSE — STATED PLAINLY SO IT IS NOT MISREAD AS COMPLETE.** **Question 2 of ADR-012 action 7 (how RED conformity interacts with CRA scope for the same product) remains OPEN**, and the RED text alone cannot answer it: this directive predates the CRA by a decade and contains no reference to it. **Still required: (i) the delegated act(s) adopted under Art 44 specifying which categories/classes are caught by 3(3)(d), (e), (f) and (i) — and whether FRMCS-class equipment is among them; (ii) any instrument postponing its application date; (iii) the OJ citation for the EN 18031 harmonised standards INCLUDING any restrictions, since a restricted citation changes what presumption of conformity is actually available; (iv) whether and when the CRA displaces the RED delegated act for products with digital elements — if one supersedes the other on a date, that date is a programme milestone ADR-012 is missing.** **(f) PROVENANCE NOTE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT BEARS ON REPEATABILITY:** `eur-lex.europa.eu` returned HTTP 403 "no matching allow rule — blocked by default deny policy" on 2026-08-16 and again on 2026-08-18 after a host-side allow was attempted; this text was supplied as a local file instead. **The register could not have verified this independently from inside the working environment, and that constraint applies to every future primary-law check.** **MOVES: YES — this is a `revise`.** **ADR-012 §Legal basis** — RED added as a **third applicable regime** alongside CRA and NIS-2, with the two-tier structure recorded; **§SCOPE GAP** block updated from "no evidentiary row" to "half-closed"; **action item 7** partially discharged, remaining scope narrowed to the delegated act. **R14 matrix evidence-ref updated** — the requirement's regulatory perimeter is materially wider than recorded 24 h ago. **R8/PR13** — CE marking + EU declaration of conformity under the RED joins CRA evidence as a bid condition (ADR-012 action 2). **ADR-001 action 8** — RED conformity assessment is a gate in the migration programme plan alongside the CCS TSI/NSA gates. **STATUS UNCHANGED: R14 stays Open** (wider scope, not a resolved one) · R7 **Accepted** · R8 **Open** · ADR-012 **Proposed**. SECURITY item → also mirrored in `evidence-log-security.md`. |

PDF distilled 2021-03-08 from source workbook `NSR_in_der_SiB1_Akt_für EBA Internet_EN.xlsx` (author metadata "HeidH"), i.e. the EBA's own web-published NSR list | National-authority register of national safety rules | Download folder `nation_safety_rules.pdf` | **A** | **R1/R2 + ADR-001 (CORRECTION)** · R7 · R13 · R14 (negative finding) | **revise** | **TIER A — the National Safety Authority's own published register of the national safety rules it administers. Primary on what the German NSR set contains.** ⚠️ **BUT SIX YEARS STALE (issue 20.08.2020)** — NSRs are amended and notified continuously; treat the *list* as indicative and re-fetch before relying on any entry. **⚠️⚠️ THIS ROW'S PRINCIPAL VALUE IS THAT IT EXPOSED AN ERROR I INTRODUCED INTO A RATIFIED ADR THREE DAYS AGO — SEE (c). THE DOCUMENT ITSELF IS OF MODEST DIRECT RELEVANCE.** **(a) WHAT IT CONTAINS.** 18 notified rules: the **AEG** (General Railway Act), **EBO** (Bau- und Betriebsordnung — "national railway technology of assets, vehicles, staff, **as far as not harmonised yet**"), **ESO 1959** (signals), the **Eisenbahn-Sicherheitsverordnung**, accident-investigation decree, two train-driver licensing/examination regulations, a tunnel fire- and civil-protection guideline ("**additional to TSI SRT** as regards national specificities"), two *Allgemeinverfügungen* on notifying dangerous incidents to the EBA, the post-2013 "**sand scattering unit**" ruling ("measure to fend off threats based on knowledge from national incidents"), UIC Loading Guidelines Vols 1–2, **VDV Scripts 755** (route knowledge / *Streckenkenntnis*), **757** (brakes in operation), **758** (freight-wagon checks), the **VDV BRW** operating regulations, and supplementary regulations **B 012** (magnetic rail brake) and **B 017** (braking on steep sections). Each carries a stated justification, mostly "transposing harmonised safety requirements" or "not harmonised yet, but accepted / proven requirements and procedures". **(b) NEGATIVE FINDING, AND IT IS A REAL ONE: NOT ONE OF THE 18 NATIONAL SAFETY RULES ADDRESSES RADIO COMMUNICATIONS, AND NOT ONE ADDRESSES CYBERSECURITY.** The set is train protection, signalling, braking, driver competence, loading, tunnels and incident reporting. **This supports the register's working picture that rail cyber obligations arrive via the TSI/CRA/NIS-2/RED route and NOT via the national safety-rule layer** — i.e. the EBA's NSR instrument is not where cyber conformance will be found, which matters for how ADR-012 is pitched and for who is asked what. Recorded as **corroboration of an absence**, which is weaker than positive evidence: a 2020 list cannot prove nothing has been added since. **(c) ⚠️ THE CORRECTION — "class B CCS system" APPEARS TWICE HERE AS THE JUSTIFICATION FOR RETAINED NATIONAL RULES (items 13 route-knowledge and 17 magnetic rail brake), WHICH PROMPTED A CROSS-CHECK THAT FOUND A MATERIAL ERROR IN ADR-001.** On **2026-08-15** I repaired ADR-001's stale "~2030 switch-off" premise and replaced it with a sourced table whose top row read: *"EU legal outer bound — **31 Dec 2040**, Class B funding option, Reg (EU) 2026/693 Art 8(2)"*, presented as the legal outer bound **for GSM-R end-of-life**. **That is wrong.** Per **E-2026-08-01-25 (tier A, ERA/UIC)**: *"RMR = two radio **Class A** systems (GSM-R + FRMCS, may coexist or independently — dual-run legal basis)"* and — decisively — *"**GSM-R continues as Class A 'without end-date'**"*. **GSM-R is Class A. The 31.12.2040 date in E-2026-08-01-11/-16 is the funding provision for CLASS B systems — the legacy NATIONAL systems (in Germany PZB/LZB and legacy analogue radio), which is exactly the sense in which this EBA document uses "class B CCS system". It does not bound GSM-R.** **(d) THE CORRECTED POSITION IS SHARPER THAN EITHER PREVIOUS VERSION: THERE IS NO EU LEGAL END-DATE FOR GSM-R AT ALL.** The register's own primary evidence says GSM-R continues as Class A *without end-date*. The horizon is therefore set by **national plan (DE switch-off 2035), ERA's obsolescence window (2035–2040), operator positioning ("mid-2030s") and vendor support commitments** — **none of which is a legal bound.** **The original ADR-001 sin (a hard ~2030 date) and my repair (a hard 2040 legal bound) are the same mistake twice: manufacturing legal certainty about a date that is not in law.** The honest statement is a planning range with no statutory backstop, and the absence of a backstop is itself the finding — it means nothing external forces the migration to complete, which *increases* the weight on R2 coexistence rather than relieving it. **(e) ⚠️ IMMEDIATE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE — THE DRAFT EBA CONSULTATION LETTER (`project/08-eba-consultation-2026-08-18.md`) CITES THE ERRONEOUS FIGURE TO THE REGULATOR:** *"31 December 2040 as the outer bound implied by the Class B funding provision"*. **The EBA administers the Class B distinction; sending them a Class A/Class B conflation would be a self-inflicted credibility loss on first contact. Corrected in the draft before sending — this row is the reason.** **(f) SECONDARY RELEVANCE, HONESTLY SCOPED:** the NSR layer is what the EBA administers nationally alongside the TSIs, so it frames what the consultation can usefully ask; items 2, 13 and 17 show national rules explicitly retained *because* harmonisation is incomplete, which is the same "national specificity vs harmonised requirement" seam the FRMCS transition sits on (**R7**). No entry bears directly on FRMCS, radio or the transition. **MOVES: YES — `revise`.** **ADR-001 §Timeline premise — the "EU legal outer bound 2040" row is WITHDRAWN and replaced** (ADR-001 is **ratified**, so this is flagged as a correction to a ratified decision's premise and must go to the ARB; the *decision* — Option B, parallel run — is unaffected). **`08-eba-consultation-2026-08-18.md` corrected.** **R1/R2 matrix evidence-ref updated.** **STATUS UNCHANGED:** R1/R2 stay **Accepted** — the correction alters the premise's legal character, not the decision. R7 Accepted · R13 Open · R14 Open · ADR-001 remains **Accepted (ARB 2026-08-15)** pending ARB notification of this premise correction. |

This is a DIFFERENT test — the national "is it MAJOR upgrading/renewal" question that gates authorisation for putting into service — with its own statutory clock.** Two tests, two authorities, one change. **(b) WHY THAT MATTERS FOR R13/ADR-009:** if an FRMCS on-board or trackside retrofit counts as *major upgrading of a structural subsystem*, **each retrofit needs an EBA authorisation for putting into service**, and the 10-week determination sits on the critical path of a ~16–21k-vehicle programme. **This row does NOT establish that it does** — the text is superseded and Annex 3 was not read. made under **ch. 7.4.4 of the Annex to Reg (EU) 2016/919** (the then-CCS TSI) | **A** | **R2** (primary) · **R1** · **R13/ADR-009** · ADR-001 (confirms the 2026-08-18 correction) | **validate** | **TIER A — the responsible federal ministry's own National Implementation Plan, a CCS TSI obligation under ch. 7.4.4 of the Annex to Reg (EU) 2016/919.** Primary on German ETCS migration policy **as it stood in December 2017**. ⚠️ **NINE YEARS STALE AND SUPERSEDED IN THREE WAYS:** its planning horizon is "bis 2023" (past); its legal basis Reg (EU) 2016/919 has been replaced by **Reg (EU) 2023/1695** (already in this register); and Digitale Schiene Deutschland plus the 2035 switch-off ambition have overtaken it. **Do not quote its plans as current.** Its value is definitional and structural, not forward-looking. **(a) ⚠️ THE HEADLINE — INDEPENDENT PRIMARY CONFIRMATION OF THE CLASS A/CLASS B CORRECTION MADE YESTERDAY (E-2026-08-18-02).** The BMVI's own abbreviation table defines: **"Class-B System | Nationales Zugsicherungssystem in Deutschland — PZB 90 oder LZB"** — *Class-B system = the national TRAIN PROTECTION system in Germany, PZB 90 or LZB.* §1.1 is titled "**Bestehende Class-B Systeme**" and contains exactly two subsections: **PZB 90** and **LZB**. **This settles it from the German side: "Class B" means legacy national train protection, NOT GSM-R.** The 31.12.2040 Class B funding provision in Reg (EU) 2026/693 therefore relates to systems of the PZB/LZB kind — **it never bounded GSM-R**, which E-2026-08-01-25 records as a **Class A** radio system "without end-date". **The ADR-001 timeline correction of 2026-08-18 is confirmed by a second, independent primary source, and the corrected EBA letter is right to drop the 2040 figure.** **(b) THE GENUINELY NEW FINDING FOR R2 — ETCS LEVEL 2 RIDES GSM-R, WHICH COUPLES THE TWO MIGRATIONS.** Paraphrased from §1.2.4: under ETCS Level 2 the train's speed is continuously supervised and **all route data relevant to the train movement is transmitted via GSM-R**, letting the on-board EVC compute a dynamic speed profile. §2.2.4 adds that fully-converted Level 2 sections need **no lineside signals but MORE GSM-R base stations**, and so cost less to operate and maintain. **CONSEQUENCE THE REGISTER HAD NOT DRAWN: on any line running ETCS Level 2, the radio layer is safety-carrying for train control, so GSM-R cannot be switched off there unless FRMCS is already carrying ETCS data. The train-protection migration and the radio migration are therefore not independent programmes — ETCS L2 rollout CONSTRAINS the GSM-R switch-off sequence, line by line.** This strengthens **R2 (coexistence)** materially and bears on the canary-by-segment design in ADR-007 and the migration sequencing in ADR-001 item 5. **(c) CLASS B SWITCH-OFF WAS EXPLICITLY NOT DECIDED — AND THE ECONOMICS POINTED THE OTHER WAY.** §3: "**Eine Abschaltung von Class B-Systemen ist bislang nicht vorgesehen**" — no switch-off of PZB/LZB was envisaged, and the plan expressly declines to decide it ("Eine Entscheidung zur Abschaltung der Class-B Systeme … wird im Rahmen des Vorhabens nicht getroffen"), deferring to results expected in 2018. Yet §2.2 records that federally commissioned research was already indicating that **faster migration with earlier switch-off of the national systems yields the better overall economic benefit**, with quantification pending. **A decision deferred, against its own emerging evidence — the same shape as the decision-drift pattern this register documented in itself.** **(d) RETROFIT PARALLELS FOR R13/ADR-009, USEFUL BECAUSE THEY ARE THE SAME PROBLEM ONE LAYER DOWN.** The cost drivers listed for on-board ETCS fitment are: supply and installation **including the GSM-R data-transmission equipment**; the need for **specific transmission modules (STM)** so ETCS vehicles can still read the Class B systems; **test, authorisation and commissioning**; maintenance; and **training of drivers and maintenance staff**. **The STM is the train-protection analogue of the hybrid GSM-R/FRMCS cab radio — dual-fitment to bridge a decade-long coexistence — and the authorisation and training lines are exactly the burdens E-2026-08-15-54 measured empirically on the cyber-retrofit side.** **(e) FRMCS IS ABSENT — ZERO OCCURRENCES IN 24 PAGES.** Dated but worth recording: as of the December 2017 national ETCS plan, **FRMCS had not entered German national implementation planning at all**, while GSM-R appears only as the assumed bearer. A datum on when the radio successor became a national planning object. **MOVES: confirms, does not change.** ADR-001's corrected timeline premise is **validated by an independent primary source** — no further edit needed. **R2 matrix evidence-ref updated** with the ETCS-L2/GSM-R coupling. **No status change:** R1/R2 stay **Accepted** · R13 **Open** · ADR-001 **Accepted (ARB 2026-08-15)** · ADR-007/-009 **Proposed**. |

| E-2026-08-18-07 | 2026-08-18 | "**Test und Nachweis KI-basierter Perzeptionssysteme bei GoA 3+: Aktuelle Forschung am DZSF**" / "Testing and validating AI-based perception systems in GoA 3+: the current research at the DZSF" — **Christian Klotz · Kristin Mühl · Prasannavenkatesh Balaji · Kai Hofmann**, **DZSF (Deutsches Zentrum für Schienenverkehrsforschung beim Eisenbahn-Bundesamt)**; **Signal + Draht 118 (6/2026)**, 8 pp, parallel German/English, © DVV Media 2026, "Autoren PDF" for dzsf.bund.de | Research-programme report by the NSA's own research centre | Download folder; **published June 2026 — the most current document in this batch** | **A** | **ADR-010** (primary) · **R11/ADR-004** · **ADR-003** · **R9/R10/ADR-002** · R5 · ADR-001 (EBA consultation) | **revise** | **TIER A, SCOPED: the DZSF is the research centre OF THE EISENBAHN-BUNDESAMT — the National Safety Authority — and these are DZSF authors reporting DZSF's own research programme. Primary as to that programme.** Same logic applied to the ERJU System Pillar deck at E-2026-08-15-53: the venue (a trade journal) does not change who wrote it or what it reports. **Scope limit, and it matters: this is primary as to DZSF's RESEARCH activities and positions. It is NOT a statement of EBA regulatory policy and must never be cited as one.** Handling: **© DVV Media 2026** — paraphrase only, never reproduce; DZSF distribution of the authors' PDF is sanctioned. **(a) ⚠️ THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SENTENCE FOR R11 AND ADR-004, FROM THE SAFETY AUTHORITY'S OWN RESEARCHERS: THE V-MODEL DOES NOT YET REACH AI.** Paraphrased: the DZSF **ATO Risk** project derived abstract safety requirements (TFFR values) for the perception and decision functions, landing between **SIL 1 and SIL 2 depending on scenario** — **but** development and validation requirements under the **V-model (EN 50716, EN 50129) cannot yet be completely derived from those values for the perception module**, because an open operating environment produces unforeseeable inputs and **it is impossible to test the algorithms against all possible input data**. They add that, unlike conventional software, **the information processing inside a neural network cannot be fully understood or assessed by humans**, and that **no standards currently describe these functionalities or the required interfaces**. **The register's R11 ("keep the safety case certifiable") has until now rested on keeping learning components OUTSIDE the certified kernel. This is the NSA's research arm confirming WHY that separation is load-bearing: for components inside the perimeter, the CENELEC assurance route does not yet close.** **(b) A NAMED REGULATORY PATHWAY THE REGISTER DID NOT HAVE — CSM-RA §2.4 "REFERENCE SYSTEM".** Paraphrased: under **CSM-RA section 2.4**, a **reference system** may be used for the approval of an AI-based perception system; if the safety level is maintained relative to **a train driver's skill-based visual perception**, use of such a system becomes possible — **but this requires data quantifying the driver's performance as the reference.** DZSF is generating exactly that: **ATO Sense** (simulator study of drivers detecting objects across speeds, object size and contrast → a model predicting driver reaction times) and the follow-on **ATO Perception** field study **running to 2028**, recording and synchronising sensor data to compare human against technical perception and to derive functional parameters such as visibility range and reaction time. **The register carries CSM-RA only as the Art 4(2) significance test (ADR-011). The risk-acceptance-by-reference-system principle is a DIFFERENT and directly relevant limb, and it is the route by which AI may actually be approved in rail.** **(c) ⚠️ THE CONTRAST THAT SHARPENS ADR-003 — THIS IS A WORKED EXAMPLE OF WHAT OUR OVERSIGHT LAYER IS NOT.** The DZSF perception module ingests sensor data, decides whether obstacle-free travel is possible, and triggers **horn, service braking or emergency braking** — it **actuates**, and is accordingly assigned **SIL 1–SIL 2**. **ADR-003's classification rests on the opposite property: our layer advises and never actuates.** This gives the register a concrete, NSA-sourced picture of a rail AI system that *is* inside the safety perimeter — **which is exactly the comparison the EBA consultation letter's Question 1 needs.** The letter can now say what we are not, against a system the addressee's own research centre has characterised. **(d) THE METHODOLOGY IS DIRECTLY TRANSPLANTABLE TO ADR-010, WHICH IS CURRENTLY BLOCKED WITH EVERY METRIC UNDEFINED.** DZSF **ATO Scenario** transfers the automotive **ODD (Operational Design Domain)** concept to rail and builds a hierarchy — **functional scenarios** (human-readable) → **logical scenarios** (parametric) → **concrete scenarios** (= test cases) — with tooling to generate them. Its stated crux is the **completeness argument**: since exhaustive testing is impossible, one must formulate **evaluable, sufficiently evident completeness criteria** and demonstrate adequate coverage of the scenario space, with the tool supplementing test cases until the criteria are met. **ATO Performance** defines per-function performance metrics (track recognition, overhead-line condition monitoring) against an ODD along the **Berlin–Dresden** route. **This is a ready-made frame for ADR-010's undefined eval metrics and for ADR-007's test surfaces — and it carries NSA-research provenance, which is worth a great deal when the eval strategy eventually goes to the NSA for ratification (ADR-010 item 5).** → new ADR-010 action item. **(e) EVALUATION FRAMING WORTH ADOPTING VERBATIM AS A CONCEPT:** DZSF splits an AI task into **"What"** (is the task solved correctly — e.g. correct classification) and **"How"** (on what basis was the decision made, which cues, can it be justified), holding that robustness requires both, since **traceability, transparency and reliability** are the practical requirements. They distinguish **explainability** (a user can understand a decision *after* being given an explanation) from **interpretability** (the model is transparent enough that experts can follow it *without* additional information, e.g. decision trees). **This maps onto ADR-002's automation-bias and dissent-rate concerns and onto ADR-010's oversight-effectiveness metrics.** Projects: **Interpretable AI** (multi-sensor RGB/infrared/LiDAR fusion, association restricted to **interpretable, physically meaningful geometric features** via decision-tree and graph-based inference; fusion filters detections not corroborated by multiple sensors — more corroborating sensors, more reliable output) and **XRAISE** (whether and how **explainable-AI methods can VERIFY** GoA 3+ perception; saliency vs concept-based methods), which has published two annotated person-detection datasets, **RailGoerl24** (RGB) and **RailGoerl25** (RGB + infrared + LiDAR). An honest sub-finding: their long-range camera scored poorly on distant objects, and they note it must be determined whether the model or the **data** is the limiting factor — hence "**it is essential to define precise requirements for the system in order to ensure a valid and realistic performance assessment**". **That is the ground-truth-gap problem ADR-010 already flags as PR8, observed independently.** **(f) NEGATIVE FINDING, RECORDED WITH ITS CAVEAT: the EU AI ACT IS NOT MENTIONED ONCE.** In eight pages published in June 2026 by the safety authority's research centre, on assuring safety-critical AI in rail, the assurance framing is **entirely CENELEC (EN 50716, EN 50129) and CSM-RA** — "AI Act", "KI-Verordnung": **zero occurrences**. **Consistent with ADR-003's conclusion that the binding route for rail AI runs through the railway safety case rather than the AI Act — but absence of mention is NOT a position, and an 8-page technical article may simply have scoped it out. Do not cite this as evidence of the EBA's AI Act stance.** **⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-19 (E-2026-08-19-05): the caveat proved necessary. Part 2 of the DZSF ATO Standortbestimmung DOES engage the AI Act directly — citing the dataset-quality requirements (Art 10(3) as numbered in the Feb-2023 draft) and stating that the KI-VO's material requirements should be reflected in future rail rulebooks. THE ABSENCE RECORDED HERE IS SPECIFIC TO THIS ARTICLE AND MUST NOT BE READ AS A DZSF POSITION.** **(g) CONTEXT LINKS:** ATO GoA 2 is being integrated into the **TSI CCS** with operation in the **Digitaler Knoten Stuttgart (DKS)**, based on **ETCS Level 2** — which E-2026-08-18-05 established transmits all route data over **GSM-R**, so the automation roadmap inherits the radio-migration dependency; GoA 3+ is where the driver's track-observation task must itself be automated. **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-010 gains an action item** (adopt the ODD/scenario-hierarchy/completeness-criteria frame and the reference-system benchmark). **ADR-004/R11 justification materially strengthened** by the NSA-sourced statement that the V-model does not yet close for AI components. **ADR-003** gains the CSM-RA §2.4 reference-system route and the actuating/non-actuating worked contrast. **EBA letter Q1 strengthened.** **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R11 stays **Proposed — load-bearing** (this informs the FFI analysis, it does not produce it) · R9/R10 **Accepted (ARB)** · ADR-010/-004 **Proposed** · ADR-003 **Accepted (ARB) — NSA concurrence outstanding**. |

Primary as to EBA/DZSF activities and stated positions — NOT a statement of regulatory requirement.** Handling: © DVV Media; the licence note permits republication of one's own contribution on the author's own inter/intranet. **Paraphrase only.** **(a) THE INSTITUTIONAL FACT WORTH HAVING: EBA AND DZSF HAVE RUN A JOINT SAFETY-CULTURE PROGRAMME SINCE 2022, AND IT FEEDS THE AUTHORISATION AND SUPERVISION PROCESSES.** Paraphrased: since 2022 the two have worked closely to build a common internal and external understanding of safety culture, with **DZSF's current research findings and empirical expertise flowing into the EBA's supervision and authorisation processes and activities** ("Aufsichts- und Genehmigungsprozesse und -aktivitäten"), and EBA practice feeding back into the research. There is a standing **internal joint Arbeitskreis Sicherheitskultur**. The day was opened by **EBA President Stefan Dernbach** and **Prof. Dr. Corinna Salander** (head of the railway division at the **BMDV**), both stressing **the decisive role of the human in railway safety**. **Session C was explicitly the view from Zulassung (authorisation) and Aufsicht (supervision)** — i.e. the exact subject matter of the pending EBA consultation. **(b) ⚠️ THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT THIS REGISTER DID NOT HAVE, AND IT BEARS DIRECTLY ON ADR-002's ACCEPTABILITY.** The closing panel converged on internal controls: all agreed they strengthen safety culture, **but only if they serve improvement and shared learning rather than pure monitoring** ("weniger um reine Überwachung"), and that acceptance depends on adapting both the *form* of such controls and *how their purpose is communicated*. **An agentic oversight layer that reads to staff as surveillance will be rejected by the safety culture it depends on, however technically sound.** ADR-002 stakes R12 on continuous monitoring and a decision-ready alert; this is the sector's own warning about how that must be framed and introduced. Recorded as a constraint on detailed design and change management — **not** a change to the ratified ADR-002 decision. **(c) THE CLOSEST REAL-WORLD COMPARATOR TO ADR-002's RISK SENTINEL — AND IT IS A HUMAN ROLE AT OUR OWN INFRASTRUCTURE MANAGER.** **Dirk Menne (Eisenbahnbetriebsleiter, DB InfraGO)** described a new role, **Fachreferent:in Betriebssicherheit**: an **independent instance** performing both document and on-site checks, relieving management in the operating districts. Its method is **digital, systematic data collection with uniform analysis**, which lets deviations and problems be identified purposefully and **long-term developments tracked** — and, notably, lets managers interact with staff **without a control function**, which they judged to improve safety culture. **This is structurally what the Risk Sentinel is proposed to do, and DB InfraGO has answered the same problem with an independent HUMAN function. The register should treat the agentic layer as augmenting that role rather than substituting for it — and it is an obvious first integration point and stakeholder.** **(d) MEASUREMENT — RELEVANT TO ADR-010 AND TO THE ENISA GAP.** Mühl, who leads DZSF's interdisciplinary safety-culture research project, presented studies on the **effects of safety-culture measures on safety INDICATORS in rail**, on **methods for evaluating those effects**, and on empirically grounded findings for sustainable implementation. **E-2026-08-15-03 recorded EU rail as LOW-maturity on "security indicators" specifically; here the safety side has an active research programme on exactly that measurement problem — a transferable method source for ADR-010's undefined oversight-effectiveness metrics.** Annette Hinze separately reported EBA's findings from **granting and supervising Safety Management Systems**. **(e) DEFINITIONAL PROVENANCE, NOTED BECAUSE IT IS A CROSS-SECTOR BORROWING:** the EBA/DZSF working definition (DZSF/EBA 2024) is **adapted from KTA 1402 (2017-11)** — a **nuclear** safety-standards guideline. Safety culture is framed as the totality of characteristics, attitudes, behaviours and behavioural expectations within a company and in individuals, determined by the safety-oriented attitude, responsibility and conduct of everyone required for railway safety. Precedent for the register's existing cross-sector borrowings (cf. the aviation comparison at the 2nd ERA-ENISA conference). **(f) SECTOR PRACTICE, RECORDED BRIEFLY AS COMPARATORS:** SBB Cargo International — safety-oriented leadership concept, **positive handling of error as learning potential**, a **Fairness-Guide**, and a low-threshold campaign ("Sei 8sam"); ÖBB Infrastruktur — leaders' on-site safety conversations, campaigns, and anchoring safety **emotionally**; and from two speakers the same emphasis on **understanding deviations from the official rulebook** rather than merely policing them. **That last point is the safety-culture analogue of this register's own finding that the informative event is the one the system did not report.** **(g) PRACTICAL BY-PRODUCT FOR THE EBA CONSULTATION — NAMED, PUBLISHED CONTACTS AT THE RIGHT LEVEL.** Unlike the generic `sg92@` address at E-2026-08-18-06, this article publishes a **Referatsleiterin (Referat 34)**, a **Referentin Sicherheitsbescheinigung** and a **stellv. Sachgebietsleiter**, plus DZSF's **Human Factors** lead — who is simultaneously the lead author on AI-perception assurance (E-2026-08-18-07). **DZSF's human-factors group therefore spans BOTH safety culture and AI assurance, which is precisely the intersection this engagement sits on.** Still not established as the FRMCS/authorisation counterpart, so the consultation note's rule stands — **do not invent an entry point** — but these are substantially better-targeted leads than anything previously on file. **MOVES: no status change — `validate`.** R12's premise is **corroborated institutionally**: the awareness/ownership gap is recognised by the authority itself and is the subject of a standing EBA/DZSF programme. **R12 matrix evidence-ref updated**; **ADR-002 action item 3 gains the not-surveillance framing constraint**.
