| E-2026-08-18-09 | 2026-08-18 | "**Cyberangriffe auf das Bahnsystem – Was bisher geschah**" (Cyber attacks on the railway system — what has happened so far): a systematic inventory of documented cyber attacks on rail sub-components — **Lukas Iffländer · Thomas Buder · Brigitte Buchetmann**; **EI – Der Eisenbahningenieur, August 2023**, 6 pp, German. Output of the **DZSF project REAVRS** ("Reducing Attack Vulnerabilities in the Rail System"), contractors **Universität der Bundeswehr München · IVE mbH · CreaLab GmbH**; homepage publication permitted for DZSF beim Eisenbahn-Bundesamt | Research-project report — dataset + method | Download folder; © DVV Media Group GmbH | **A** | **R14/ADR-012** (primary) · **R12** · **R8/PR13** · **R13/PR14** · R3/R4 | **validate** | **TIER A, SAME SCOPING AS E-2026-08-18-07/-08:** a research output of the **DZSF — the research centre of the Eisenbahn-Bundesamt** — with a named academic contractor, publishing its **method and its dataset**. Primary as to the REAVRS project's methodology and results. **Not** a threat assessment issued by the authority, and not to be cited as one. ⚠️ **Three years old; the dataset ends October 2021** — it predates the 23 June 2026 incident and everything the register has logged since. **(a) ⚠️ THE MOST USEFUL THING IT DOES IS LET THE REGISTER RETIRE A BAD NUMBER.** At **E-2026-08-15-54** the register logged RazorSecure's "**391% increase in portscans + denial of service, 2022–2024**" and flagged it as **uncitable** — measured on the vendor's own install base, no denominator, no methodology. **This row supplies the defensible alternative: a stated method, a published dataset, named sources and self-declared limitations.** Where a client deck needs a rail threat characterisation, this is what it should rest on. **(b) THE HEADLINE FINDING, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THE PREVAILING SALES NARRATIVE: "the MAJORITY of attacks have so far had NO DIRECT EFFECT ON RAILWAY OPERATIONS."** Of **31 systematically recorded attacks** (2018-05 to 2021-10), the dominant pattern is **IT-side, not OT-side**: roughly **40% are extortion attempts**, ransomware the favoured method — and the authors note that in many cases data is **not encrypted but simply deleted**. Affected systems in their schema are overwhelmingly ticketing/payment, station IT, websites, passenger information, internal communication and disposition — with "Bahnbetrieb" (rail operations) the exception rather than the rule. **In only ~30% of cases is there a suspected or proven perpetrator.** **This refines ADR-012's threat framing rather than overturning it: the realistic near-term exposure is IT-side extortion and data loss, while OT-side operational compromise remains the low-frequency/high-consequence tail. Both belong in the risk register, but they should not be argued as though they were the same threat.** No ADR edit made — the decision is unaffected, only its supporting characterisation is sharpened. **(c) ⚠️ THE METHODOLOGY IS TRANSPARENT, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY IT MUST BOUND THE FINDING — THE COUNT IS A FLOOR, NOT A CENSUS.** The search was conducted **essentially via Google**, with **English-language search terms** ("cyber", "attack", "rail", "transport", "hacker") in varying combinations, seeded from four secondary compilations: the **ENISA Railway Cybersecurity report** (already in this register), a **CSIS** list of significant cyber events since 2006, a **University of Alabama** transport-sector list, and a list from the consultancy **KonBriefing.com**. The authors state plainly that experts assume an **immense Dunkelziffer** (unreported cases) and that some entries rest on the assertions of intelligence services or IT-security firms. **They also explain their own regional skew rather than presenting it as a result: the concentration in English-speaking countries is attributed to LINGUISTIC ACCESSIBILITY — English being the standard language of computing, the pool of capable attackers is larger — not to those railways being more vulnerable.** Ukraine's elevated count is contextualised against the occupation of Crimea and pre-2022-invasion pressure; China exceeding India despite similar population is attributed to **stronger digitalisation** (many recently built lines) versus Indian infrastructure dating to British administration. **Read as: 31 is what English-language open sources surfaced by 2021, not what happened.** **(d) THE ONE DOCUMENTED OT ATTACK WITH PHYSICAL HARM — AND IT IS THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE TO THIS REGISTER'S OWN FAIL-SAFE ARGUMENT.** The article notes the **Łódź tram case (Poland, 2008)**: a **14-year-old** manipulated **point setting** using an **infrared remote control**, **derailing four tram vehicles and injuring several people**. **This matters for the SIM-SEC-001 precedent.** There the register held — correctly — that malicious triggering of a *fail-safe* (the RADIO-STOP emergency braking case) is an **availability** loss, **not** T0880 Loss of Safety. **Łódź is the opposite case: manipulating a non-vital control path to command an UNSAFE state produced derailment and injury.** The distinction the register must keep is therefore **not** "attacks on rail are only availability events" but **"triggering a fail-safe is an availability event; subverting a control path to command an unsafe state is not."** Recorded against SIM-SEC-001 so the precedent is not over-generalised. (Tram system, non-vital IR control — not directly transferable to a SIL-4 interlocking, but the analytical point stands.) **(e) FOUR SECTOR CHALLENGES THE AUTHORS REPORT AS IDENTIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BY BOTH ENISA AND DZSF — AND ALL FOUR MAP ONTO REQUIREMENTS THIS REGISTER ALREADY CARRIES:** (1) during digital transformation, a balance must be struck between **competitiveness, operational requirements and cybersecurity**; (2) railway undertakings depend on **a large number of suppliers over whose cybersecurity they have little influence** → **R8/PR13**, ADR-012 action 2; (3) **long-lived operational technology has difficulty being compatible with modern cybersecurity requirements** → **R13/PR14**, and precisely the 1991-node problem; (4) **staff culture in rail has so far engaged little with cybersecurity questions** → **R12**, and the direct security-side counterpart to the safety-culture programme at E-2026-08-18-08; plus (5) **existing regulatory requirements take cybersecurity into account only to a small extent** — **the same defect the ESCG named at E-2026-08-15-19, here stated by the safety authority's own research centre.** Context: BSI rated the IT-security situation **"angespannt bis kritisch"** with ~319,000 new malware variants daily. **(f) OPEN FOLLOW-UP:** the authors state that **detailed per-attack information would be published after project completion, expected Q4/2023.** Three years on, **the register does not have it.** Chase the REAVRS final publication — it would be the first primary, per-incident rail attack dataset in this register and would supersede this summary. **MOVES: no status change — `validate`.** R14's premise is corroborated *and bounded*. **R14 matrix evidence-ref updated**; **SIM-SEC-001 annotated** with the Łódź counter-example. R14 **Open** · R12 **Proposed** · R8/R13 **Open** · ADR-012 **Proposed**. SECURITY item → mirrored in `evidence-log-security.md`. |

| E-2026-08-19-01 | 2026-08-19 | "**Automation Myth #4 — Automation disenfranchises the human operator, making a teaming between humans and automation impossible**" / *New form of teamwork: Teaming between humans and automation* — **Dr Michèle Rieth**, Dept. of Business Psychology & Human Resource Management, **Universität Bremen**; **ERA–DZSF "Automation Myths" series, February 2023**, 5 pp, English. PDF authored by **Kristin Mühl** (DZSF Human Factors — the same lead as E-2026-08-18-07 and -08). Rail transfer credited to Justin Adam and Alexander Schulz | Agency/research-centre publication series — human-factors synthesis | Download folder `2023_02_ERA-DZSF_MP4_EN.pdf` | **A** | **ADR-002** (primary) · **R10** · **ADR-004** · **ADR-010** · R9 | **revise** | **TIER A — jointly published by the EU Agency for Railways and the DZSF (the EBA's research centre), i.e. the same two institutions whose positions this register has been tracking, writing on human-automation teaming.** Primary as an ERA/DZSF publication and as to Rieth's own position. ⚠️ **Scope limit: the substantive content is a LITERATURE SYNTHESIS, and the teaming model is second-hand — derived from an international expert interview study (Rieth & Hagemann 2022) that is cited, not reproduced here.** Treat the model as a well-sourced design heuristic, not as validated data. **(a) ⚠️ THE HEADLINE — THE REGISTER NOW HAS A NAMED, DOCUMENTED FAILURE MODE FOR EXACTLY WHAT ADR-002 PROPOSES, FROM AN ADJACENT SAFETY-CRITICAL DOMAIN.** The opening case is air traffic control's **Arrival Manager**: an advisory system that generates optimal approach sequences from flight path, speed and runway conditions — **structurally the same thing as ADR-002's advisory agents.** Paraphrased outcome: what was seen as a beneficial advance is now perceived negatively by some controllers, who **feel disenfranchised**; the active, creative work of making a sequence out of the "traffic clutter" moved to the system, leaving them to **check the machine's sequence in a time-consuming manner and implement it more or less passively**. The implementation did not consider that it automated **the part of the job the operators most identify with**, and the holistic effects on the combined human+automation system were never assessed — producing job dissatisfaction, declining motivation and, consequently, **reduced performance**. **ADR-002's ladder (Audit → Supervise → Approve → Command) is precisely a design in which the machine proposes and the human checks. This is the documented consequence of that shape when it is not deliberately designed against.** **(b) THE MECHANISM HAS A NAME, AND NAMING IT IS THE USEFUL PART: THE "LEFT-OVER PRINCIPLE".** Rieth contrasts a **technology-centred** approach — automate everything a machine does more accurately, efficiently or reliably, and **whatever remains falls to the human** — with a **human-centred** approach, where automation compensates for human limitations or extends human capability, and **"it is not always reasonable to automate everything that leads to more efficiency"**, costs and benefits being assessed holistically. The technology-centred route yields **passive, monotonous residual tasks** → inattentiveness, demotivation, performance loss. **This is a direct constraint on how the agent set is scoped: what the agents take must not be chosen merely by what they can do well.** **(c) THE DESIGN SPECIFICATION — TRANSPLANTABLE ALMOST LINE BY LINE INTO ADR-002 AND ADR-010.** From the teaming model: **human side** — the operator must hold **system knowledge: the system's logic, capabilities AND limitations**; **automation side** — it must **work safely and reliably** (or trust and willingness to use it collapse), its **behaviour, mode and intentions must be made transparent through the interface**, and it should **explain the reasons behind an automated decision comprehensibly**; **both** — they must share an understanding of the **overall work target**, be able to **mutually estimate current and future (mental) states**, and have **function allocation assigned to human strengths and flexibly adjustable to the situation**. **The explainability and transparency requirements here arrive at the same place as the DZSF's AI-assurance work (E-2026-08-18-07) from the opposite direction — that paper wanted explainability to VERIFY the system; this one wants it to keep the human genuinely in the loop. Both point at the same interface obligation.** **(d) ⚠️ THE MOST VALUABLE PARAGRAPH FOR ADR-004 — AN OPERATING PRECEDENT FOR THE SIL-4 BOUNDARY, ALREADY RUNNING ON GERMAN RAILWAYS.** Paraphrased: in electronic interlockings, **automatic route setting (ARS)** already performs **decision selection AND action execution** — it sets routes for trains in the control plan from pre-entered data, defaulting to **first-come-first-served**, and where the safety-relevant conditions are met **the interlocking sets the route and lets the train run**. **But — and this is the load-bearing part — "due to safety standards, the train control system acts SEPARATELY from the disposition system" and "usually has NO ACCESS to current timetable and delay data."** Consequently, when delays cause conflicts, first-come-first-served is **not always appropriate**, and **manual disposition by the signaller is required** (deactivating/reactivating train control at individual signals, editing the routing plan); in malfunctions the system **is not permitted to continue automatically** and the human takes over. **This is ADR-004's boundary as a live, operating arrangement rather than a proposal — the safety-carrying system is deliberately isolated from the optimisation data — and it reframes ADR-002's value proposition precisely: the separation ITSELF creates an information gap that only the human currently spans. An advisory layer that reads disposition data and informs the signaller is filling exactly that gap, WITHOUT crossing the boundary. That is a sharper and more defensible statement of what the oversight layer is for than "closing the awareness gap", and it should go into the EBA consultation.** **(e) "A STANDING TRAIN IS A SAFE TRAIN" — AN INDEPENDENT ARTICULATION OF THE PRINCIPLE THIS REGISTER HAS BEEN RELYING ON.** Rieth explains why rail automates action execution further than ATC does: rail movement is two-dimensional and **has a safe state in standstill**, whereas in the air no equivalent safe state exists, so a higher degree of action-implementation automation **is not currently aimed for in ATC**. She also notes ARS only functions where train data exist and technical security is complete — otherwise **signals remain at hold and traffic stops until humans intervene**. **This is the same fail-safe logic the register applies at SIM-SEC-001 and E-2026-07-02-34 (radio loss → forced service brake), here stated as the design rationale that LICENSES rail's higher automation. It cuts both ways and both should be recorded: the safe state is what permits automation, and it is also why so many failure modes surface as availability loss rather than harm.** **(f) THE COUNTERMEASURE, AND IT IS CHEAP: FLEXIBLE FUNCTION ALLOCATION INCLUDING DELIBERATE PRACTICE.** Rieth's proposed remedy for disenfranchisement is to let operators **flexibly allocate functions between themselves and the automation as needed** — the example given is that the Arrival Manager assists in stressful traffic, while **in calm traffic, and for the purpose of REGULAR PRACTICE, the human performs the task themselves**. **Deliberately handing the task back to maintain skill is a concrete design requirement, and the register has nothing on automation-induced skill decay.** → ADR-002 and ADR-010 (which already carries automation-bias and dissent-rate metrics but no skill-retention measure). **(g) THE GAP RIETH IDENTIFIES IN CURRENT RAIL AUTOMATION IS AN INTERFACE GAP:** while automation already relieves signallers of extensive simple tasks in regular operation, **"the transparency of train control in the sense of communication of the planned and next executed actions could still be improved."** A requirement the oversight layer should meet from the outset rather than inherit. **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-002 action item 3 extended** with the left-over-principle constraint, the teaming-model design requirements and flexible function allocation with practice. **ADR-004 gains the ARS/disposition separation as an operating precedent.** **ADR-010** to add a skill-retention measure alongside automation-bias metrics. **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R9/R10 **Accepted (ARB)** · R11 **Proposed — load-bearing** · ADR-002/-003 **Accepted (ARB) — NSA concurrence outstanding** · ADR-004/-010 **Proposed**. |

| E-2026-08-19-02 | 2026-08-19 | "**Standortbestimmung des DZSF zum Thema ATO — Teil 1: Grundlagen und Sicherheitsanforderungen**" (DZSF position on ATO, Part 1: fundamentals and safety requirements) — **Kai Hofmann · Rustam Tagiew · Roman Tilly · Christian Klotz · Markus Reinhardt**, **DZSF**; **EI – Der Eisenbahningenieur, January 2023**, 4 pp, German. Homepage publication permitted for DZSF beim Eisenbahn-Bundesamt | **Position statement** (*Standortbestimmung*) of the NSA's research centre | Download folder; © DVV Media Group GmbH. **Part 1 of a series — Part 2 is NOT in this register** | **A** | **ADR-002** (primary) · **ADR-010** · **ADR-004/R11** · **ADR-003** · **R9** · ADR-011 | **revise** | **TIER A — and this row settles a scoping question the register had been answering by inference.** The article states DZSF's status explicitly: **a departmental research institution of the BMDV, organisationally integrated into the Eisenbahn-Bundesamt — "die hier dargestellte Perspektive ist dennoch diejenige der FORSCHUNG, nicht notwendigerweise die des Bundes und des EBA"** (the perspective presented is that of research, **not necessarily that of the Federal Government or the EBA**). **That is DZSF's own disclaimer, and it confirms the scope limit this register has been applying to E-2026-08-18-07/-08/-09 and E-2026-08-19-01 — now sourced rather than assumed. DZSF material is primary as to DZSF research and positions; it is NOT EBA regulatory policy, and no DZSF document in this register may be cited as such.** **(a) ⚠️ THE FIRST-ORDER FINDING, AND THE REGISTER HAS NEVER ASKED THE QUESTION: THE APPROVABILITY OF AN AI SYSTEM TURNS ON WHETHER IT IS "VOLLSTÄNDIG PRÜFBAR" — FULLY VERIFIABLE BEFORE COMMISSIONING.** Paraphrased: for safety assessment, the essential distinction among AI systems is **whether their computed results and decisions are fully checkable prior to entry into service**. Full checkability is achievable where **the decision rules can be traced**, or where **decision behaviour can be verified as correct across all input parameters**. It is **frequently NOT achievable for systems whose decision behaviour is learned from training data by machine learning** — and expressly **not for deep neural networks**, which have proven very capable (image recognition, text analysis, translation) but **escape complete verification because of their complex and extensive structure**. **THE PAYOFF IS STATED PLAINLY: the basic functions for securing train movement (BF1) and controlling train movement (BF2) can be implemented with FULLY VERIFIABLE AI systems — "usually simply called software" — and ARE APPROVABLE WITHIN THE EXISTING LEGAL FRAMEWORK. It is BF3, checking the route is free of external obstacles, that demands a technical system monitor the train's environment and react as the driver currently does by visual inspection and human intelligence — and that is where full verifiability fails.** **CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ENGAGEMENT: whether the agentic oversight layer is approvable under existing law may turn less on WHERE it sits than on WHAT IT IS BUILT FROM. A rules-traceable or exhaustively-verifiable implementation is, on DZSF's reading, already approvable; a deep-learning implementation is not, and would push the layer into the same unresolved territory as BF3 perception. ADR-002 specifies agents and ADR-010 an eval harness, but NEITHER constrains the implementation class. That is now an open architectural decision, not an implementation detail.** → new ADR-002 action item. **(b) A THIRD CSM-RA LIMB — AND THE ONE THAT APPLIES WHEN THERE IS NO PRECEDENT TO LEAN ON.** Paraphrased: hazards are determined via the risk-assessment procedure of **CSM-RA Reg (EU) 402/2013**, with the exact process and level of detail depending on **which risk-acceptance principle is used (CSM-RA 2.1.4)** — and **"in the absence of relevant codes of practice or technical reference systems, EXPLICIT risk estimation must be applied."** Hazards are then structured into failure scenarios with safety measures defined (2.1.6); the residual risk is estimated and compared against a risk-acceptance criterion; **the selected safety measures are taken into the system definition AS SAFETY REQUIREMENTS.** **The register now holds three distinct CSM-RA limbs and should stop treating "CSM-RA" as one thing: Art 4(2) SIGNIFICANCE (ADR-011), §2.4 REFERENCE SYSTEM (E-2026-08-18-07 — the route DZSF proposes for AI perception), and 2.1.4 EXPLICIT RISK ESTIMATION, which is the fallback precisely where our agentic layer sits: no code of practice, no technical reference system.** **(c) THE SYSTEM-DEFINITION REQUIREMENT — CONCRETE AND ACTIONABLE FOR ADR-004.** Safety and function investigations require a system description **claiming completeness and delimitation**; under the CENELEC standards or CSM-RA the object of assessment is fixed by defining the system's **purpose, boundaries and environmental conditions**. The focus is rail operation with its basic functions and protection goals, and — importantly — **irrespective of which tasks fall to vehicle, infrastructure, LST or ATO, the risks must ultimately be controlled.** DZSF's **ATO Risk** project produced a **generic system definition at system level using DIN VDE V 0831-101 and DIN VDE V 0831-103**, whose stated advantage is characterising the system **largely independently of the technical realisation**. **That is a directly usable template for ADR-004's outstanding boundary specification, and it names two standards the register does not carry.** **(d) THE GoA TAXONOMY IS BORROWED AND DOES NOT FIT MAINLINE RAIL — STATED BY THE NSA'S OWN RESEARCHERS.** GoA 0–4 originates in **urban rail (BOStrab §1(2) no. 2)** and applies to independent railways structurally separated from other traffic — U-Bahn and Hochbahn. **On mainline railways under European regulation and the EBO these terms "cannot be transferred unquestioned", and automation levels are used INCONSISTENTLY in rail.** European state of the art is **"ATO over ETCS", corresponding to GoA 2 on open line**; running driverless in a depot (Hamburg) does not by itself raise the system to GoA 4. DZSF explicitly rejects intermediate inventions such as **"GoA 2.5"** and **"GoA 2+"** as merely generating confusion, classifying such concepts as fully-achieved **GoA 2**; **GoA 3+** is used as shorthand for levels 3 and 4 combined. **DZSF's proposed reframing is the useful part: decouple the GoA classification from the train driver and ask instead WHICH BASIC FUNCTIONS MUST STILL BE COVERED BY A HUMAN — whether on the vehicle or elsewhere — treating the technical realisation as secondary.** The four basic functions (abstracted from **DIN EN 62267**): **BF1** secure train movement (PZB/LZB) · **BF2** control train movement, accelerate and brake (ETCS) · **BF3** route free of external obstacles (image processing, e.g. persons on track) · **BF4** operate the train (doors, brake test, emergencies). **This function-allocation frame is the same move E-2026-08-19-01 makes for human-automation teaming, and it is a better basis for describing our oversight layer to a regulator than any autonomy label.** **(e) A DEFINITION OF AUTONOMY WORTH ADOPTING, BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE THE AUTHORITY'S RESEARCHERS USE.** DZSF uses *automatisiert* and *automatisch* synonymously for ATO, and defines **autonomy as the ability of an entity to operate WITHIN A DEFINED TASK AREA without active and necessary interventions by other entities.** Their worked example: if trackside sensors detect foreign objects and stop the vehicle (Nuremberg U-Bahn), that is **automated**; a vehicle carrying its own sensors and **making the decision on board brakes AUTONOMOUSLY**. **R9 is "keep autonomy governable" — this supplies the register's first authority-sourced definition of the term, and it is a BOUNDED-ENVELOPE definition, consistent with ADR-002's decision-class model and with the CTMS constrained-envelope pattern at E-2026-07-02-05.** **(f) FOLLOW-UPS:** **Part 2 of this Standortbestimmung is not in the register** — obtain it; and the planned project **"Einsatzszenarien ATO"** was to deliver a systematic scenario set **for the development AND Zulassung of AI for ATO**, which would bear directly on ADR-010 item 5. Neither is confirmed. **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-002 gains an action item** on constraining the agents' implementation class to fully-verifiable methods, or explicitly accepting the approvability consequence of not doing so. **ADR-004 gains** the CSM-RA 2.1.4 explicit-risk-estimation route and the generic-system-definition template (DIN VDE V 0831-101/-103). **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R9/R10 **Accepted (ARB)** · R11 **Proposed — load-bearing** · ADR-002/-003 **Accepted (ARB) — NSA concurrence outstanding** · ADR-004/-010/-011 **Proposed**. |

| E-2026-08-19-03 | 2026-08-19 | "**Rückblick auf die DZSF-Fachkonferenz Cybersecurity-Forschung**" — report on the **DZSF cybersecurity research conference, 13 October 2022 (online)** — **Kristin Mühl · Martin Lehnert · Lukas Iffländer** (DZSF); **EI – Der Eisenbahningenieur, December 2022**, 5 pp, German | Conference report — NSA research centre's own event | Download folder; © DVV Media Group GmbH | **A** | **R12** (primary) · **R14/ADR-012** · **ADR-007** · R8 | **validate** | **TIER A — DZSF staff reporting DZSF's own conference and its own commissioned projects.** Per the explicit disclaimer recorded at E-2026-08-19-02, this is the **research** perspective, not EBA policy. Opened by **Prof. Dr. Corinna Salander, then Direktorin des DZSF** — the same person who by the 2024 safety-culture event (E-2026-08-18-08) is **Abteilungsleiterin Eisenbahn im BMDV**; noted because the register should not read her two appearances as two independent institutional voices. **(a) ⚠️ A DOCUMENTED ATTACK ON RAIL TELECOMMUNICATIONS THAT THIS REGISTER DOES NOT HOLD.** Salander framed the conference against "**die Sabotage der Telekommunikationsinfrastruktur der Deutschen Bahn AG**" — the **October 2022 sabotage of DB's telecommunications infrastructure**. **Checked: the register has NOTHING on it.** "Sabotage" appears only in relation to the 23 June 2026 outage being *not* sabotage, in UIC all-hazards framing, in ENISA's scenario list and in political rhetoric. **This is a physical attack on rail TELECOMS infrastructure with direct operational effect — the closest real-world analogue to this engagement's own incident, and to the FRMCS bearer's exposure. It also qualifies the E-2026-08-18-09 finding that "the majority of attacks had no direct effect on rail operations": this one did.** → follow-up: obtain a primary account (BNetzA/BKA/DB or the Bundestag record) and log it against **R3/R4/R14**. **(b) THE MATURITY FINDING, AND IT CORROBORATES ENISA BY A DIFFERENT METHOD.** Project "**Security und geplanter Technologieeinsatz**" (Prof. Dr. Dietmar Möller, TU Clausthal) surveyed rail companies against the **NIST framework — Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover.** Result paraphrased: **all companies have implemented cybersecurity measures, but in very different degrees; on average a RATHER LOW MATURITY LEVEL.** **E-2026-08-15-03 recorded ENISA's EU-wide 2019-20 survey finding rail HIGH on logging and LOW on detection. This is a German-sector survey, different instrument, same direction — the maturity gap is now corroborated across two independent studies.** R12/R14 justification strengthened; **status unchanged**. **(c) THE BINDING CONSTRAINT NAMED IN THE PANEL IS PEOPLE, NOT TECHNOLOGY.** Paraphrased: awareness exists in the rail sector, **but far too little personnel is available, and building up that personnel is an urgent task.** **The register has treated R12 as an information problem and R14 as a conformance problem; this says the limiting factor is staffing. That bears on every ADR-012 action item — an SBOM regime, a CVD contact, an expedited-vulnerability path and a security test surface all presuppose people to run them — and on whether an agentic layer is a substitute for absent staff or a multiplier for scarce staff. It is the latter (oversight, not control), and the distinction should be explicit when this is presented.** **(d) ADR-012's CENTRAL TENSION, ARTICULATED INDEPENDENTLY IN 2022.** **Prof. Dr. Stefan Katzenbeisser (Universität Passau):** maintaining permanent IT security is a challenge **because cybersecurity cannot be demonstrated once, at project design and construction, for all time.** **That is precisely ADR-012's load-bearing trade — CRA mandates updates across a support period while railway authorisation prizes stability — stated by an academic at the NSA's own research conference four years before this register framed it.** Corroboration, not novelty; recorded because it shows the tension is sector-recognised rather than an artefact of our framing. **(e) LST SECURITY HAS A LONGER HISTORY THAN THE REGISTER ASSUMED.** A panellist (Braunschweig) noted that **threat analyses for software applications and communication systems in Leit- und Sicherungstechnik have been performed for over ten years**, and that systems already exist — **a project in Norway was cited** — realising **rail-grade applications with an appropriate safety integrity level for LST communication over IP networks**. Caution added: cybersecurity must not be secured only in individual lighthouse projects for new systems. **A precedent worth chasing for ADR-004/ADR-012 — secure IP-based LST communication at a stated SIL is the same problem class as carrying ETCS over FRMCS.** **(f) THE THREE DZSF PROJECTS, spanning three time horizons** — current state (Möller, above) · **REAVRS** (Univ. der Bundeswehr München — the project behind **E-2026-08-18-09**, here systematising **attack potentials** via vignettes, covering cyber, organisation, voice/data communication **and physical interventions**) · **"Prognose Securitybedarf…"** (see **E-2026-08-19-04**), whose software-supported **threat analysis by ATTACK GRAPHS** was presented by **Dr. Markus Heinrich, Incyde GmbH**, collecting the possible **abuse cases** for each use case. **MOVES: no status change — `validate`.** R12/R14 corroborated; the October 2022 DB sabotage logged as an evidence **gap**, not as evidence. R12 **Proposed** · R14/R8 **Open** · ADR-007/-012 **Proposed**. SECURITY item → mirrored. |
| E-2026-08-19-04 | 2026-08-19 | "**Technologie- und Securityprognose System Bahn – Bedrohungen rechtzeitig erkennen**" / *Technology and security forecast for the railway system — the timely identification of threats* — **Markus Heinrich** (Incyde GmbH) · **Lukas Iffländer** (**DZSF**, Scientific Consultant Cyber Security) · **Dirk Scheuermann** (**Fraunhofer SIT**) · **Stefan Katzenbeisser** (Univ. Passau) · **Simon Unger** (Univ. Passau); **Signal + Draht 114 (09/2022)**, 8 pp, parallel German/English. Output of the DZSF-commissioned and DZSF-financed project "**Prognose Securitybedarf und Bewertung möglicher Sicherheitskonzepte für das System Bahn**"; DOI 10.48755/dzsf.220008.06 | DZSF-funded research paper | Download folder; © DVV Media Group GmbH | **A** | **ADR-007** (primary) · **ADR-012/R14** · R8/PR13 · ADR-010 | **revise** | **TIER A — a DZSF-commissioned and DZSF-financed research output with a DZSF staff co-author, published with a DZSF DOI.** Research perspective, not EBA policy (E-2026-08-19-02 disclaimer applies). Named institutional co-authors at **Fraunhofer SIT** and **Universität Passau** strengthen it; **Incyde GmbH is a commercial security consultancy**, so the tooling it authored is noted as its own product — though **published open-source**, which materially reduces the concern. **(a) ⚠️ THE METHOD IS DIRECTLY USABLE FOR ADR-007 ITEM 7, WHICH IS CURRENTLY AN EMPTY REQUIREMENT.** ADR-007 gained a "security test surface" item on 2026-08-15 with nothing behind it. This supplies a concrete, rail-specific, published method: **forecast how digital technologies will be used, derive ABUSE CASES (how they can be misused by attacks), and build software-supported threat analysis by ATTACK GRAPHS** — the tool collecting, for each use case considered, the possible abuse cases into a graph. **The software is freely available on GitHub (`incyde-gmbh/drawio-plugin-attackgraphs`, `INCYDE-GmbH/attackgraphs`)** and the method is written up separately in Signal+Draht 05/2022 (not in this register — obtain). **This is the first concrete, cite-able security-test methodology in the register, and it comes with tooling.** → ADR-007 item 7. **(b) A VALIDATION TECHNIQUE WORTH STEALING FOR ADR-010.** For the detailed risk analysis the project has **two teams of experts perform SEPARATE investigations and compare their results against one another**, deriving protection requirements from the reconciled output. **ADR-010's eval strategy has no inter-rater or independent-replication provision; this is a cheap, defensible one, and it is the analytical analogue of the adversarial-verification discipline this register already applies to its own findings.** **(c) THE FRAMING QUESTION IS THE ONE ADR-012 SHOULD BE ASKING.** Paraphrased: **CLC/TS 50701 has existed since 2021**, closely based on **IEC 62443** (originally developed for industrial automation), and the norms represent the current state of the art — **but cybersecurity develops dynamically and new attack techniques keep arriving, so it must be examined whether the normatively-fixed measures can also ward off EXPECTED FUTURE threats.** Their stated procedure: **first consider the existing standards applicable to rail, then IDENTIFY GAPS, then develop targeted measures to close them**, with iterative risk reassessment. **ADR-012 currently treats TS 50701/IEC 62443 (migrating to IEC 63452) as the conformance target. This reframes the standards as a floor to be gap-analysed rather than a ceiling to be met — which is the right posture for a system with a 20-year asset life, and it is the same instinct as ADR-012's own "to revisit" discipline.** **(d) POST-QUANTUM — CORROBORATES THE REGISTER'S EXISTING THREAD AND NAMES THE GERMAN REFERENCE.** Paraphrased: quantum computers are **not currently a significant threat** (too few qubits), but worldwide research could make them one, so **system designers must ensure sufficiently cryptographically solid procedures now so that future quantum computers do not endanger them** — and **the BSI's post-quantum cryptography recommendations, based on the current state of the art, can be used for this.** **The register already carries harvest-now-decrypt-later, crypto-agility and NIST FIPS 203/204/205; this adds the GERMAN authority's recommendation as the applicable reference and is a ready-made question for the pending ACS enquiry (`project/09-acs-enquiry-2026-08-18.md`), which already asks BSI about TR-03183.** **(e) A STANDARD THE REGISTER DOES NOT CARRY:** **DIN VDE V 0831-104**, "Leitfaden für die IT-Sicherheit auf Grundlage IEC 62443" (2015) — the German rail-signalling IT-security guide. With **DIN VDE V 0831-101 and -103** named at E-2026-08-19-02 for the ATO Risk system definition, the register now has three instruments from this series and **none of their texts**. → obtain. **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-007 item 7 gains a concrete method** (abuse cases + attack graphs + open tooling) and **ADR-010 an inter-rater provision**; **ADR-012 gains the standards-as-floor gap-analysis framing** and the BSI PQC reference. **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R14/R8 **Open** · ADR-007/-010/-012 **Proposed**. SECURITY item → mirrored. |

| E-2026-08-19-05 | 2026-08-19 | "**Standortbestimmung des DZSF zum Thema ATO — Teil 2: Sicherheitsnachweis für KI-Komponenten und aktuelle DZSF-Projekte im Bereich ATO**" — **Kai Hofmann · Rustam Tagiew · Roman Tilly · Christian Klotz · Markus Reinhardt** (DZSF); **EI – Der Eisenbahningenieur, February 2023**, 2 pp, German. **Part 2 of the series begun at E-2026-08-19-02** — the follow-up that row flagged as missing | **Position statement** of the NSA's research centre | Download folder; © DVV Media Group GmbH | **A** | **R11/ADR-004** (primary) · **ADR-010** · **ADR-002** · **ADR-003** · R9 | **revise** | **TIER A — DZSF position statement, carrying the same explicit disclaimer as Part 1: the perspective is that of RESEARCH, not necessarily that of the Federal Government or the EBA.** **(a) ⚠️ THE SINGLE MOST DIRECT STATEMENT IN THIS REGISTER ON WHY LEARNING COMPONENTS MUST STAY OUTSIDE THE CERTIFIED KERNEL — AND IT COMES FROM THE SAFETY AUTHORITY'S OWN RESEARCHERS.** Paraphrased: **for ML-based image-processing systems, an ANALYTICAL PROOF that excludes errors on UNKNOWN input parameters on the basis of KNOWN input parameters is NOT POSSIBLE. An autonomous train could therefore SYSTEMATICALLY CAUSE ACCIDENTS as a result of undetected errors.** **R11 ("keep the safety case certifiable") and ADR-004's separation have rested on an architectural judgement. This is that judgement stated as a technical impossibility by DZSF — not that verification is hard, but that the analytical route is unavailable in principle. It is the strongest available support for the guardrail and should be quoted in the EBA consultation.** **(b) ⚠️ A CORRECTION TO THIS REGISTER, AND IT IS MINE.** At **E-2026-08-18-07** I recorded as a negative finding that the EU AI Act is **"not mentioned once"** in the DZSF GoA 3+ perception article, with the caveat that absence of mention is not a position. **That caveat was necessary: Part 2 of the very same series DOES engage the AI Act directly.** Paraphrased: **the material requirements of the KI-VO should be taken into account in future rail rulebooks (citing Art. 79)**, and specifically **training, validation and test datasets must be "relevant, representative, error-free and complete" (citing Art. 10(3))**, must cover the functions fixed in the system definition across the operational scenarios and environmental conditions, and **must also cover unusual, irregular or even DELIBERATELY DAMAGING scenarios** so that ML-based ATO functions still produce correct results and decisions in them. **⚠️ Article numbering is as cited in February 2023, i.e. against the then-DRAFT AI Regulation; Art 10(3) corresponds to the data-governance provision in the adopted Reg (EU) 2024/1689, but the Art 79 reference must NOT be assumed to map onto the final numbering — unverified, and primary law is not fetchable from this environment. The E-2026-08-18-07 note is annotated accordingly: the absence there was article-specific and must not be generalised into a DZSF position.** **(c) THE DATA TAXONOMY — DIRECTLY ACTIONABLE FOR ADR-010, WHICH STILL HAS NO METRICS.** Safety assessment of ML-based functions needs **at least three kinds of data**: **D1** case combinations of input parameters and correct results; **D2** event probabilities for certain groups of input parameters; **D3** evaluations of certain groups of failure modes, i.e. the discrepancy between the ML-computed result and the correct result for given inputs. Worked for BF3 environment monitoring: **D1** = sensor data from the track environment plus labelling of the objects detected in it; **D2** = probability of persons in particular areas of the sensor data; **D3** = damage severity arising from misdetection of a person. **The load-bearing relationship: D1 is needed to TRAIN and VERIFY, while D2 and D3 are needed to STEER the D1 collection — deliberately seeking the case combinations where a failure would cause serious damage — and to demonstrate a sufficient safety level. In other words the risk model drives the data collection, not the other way round.** And stated plainly: **"the extent of the required test scenarios and data is currently not known."** **(d) TEST METHODS AND TWO STANDARDS THE REGISTER DOES NOT CARRY.** ML systems can be tested where inputs and desired results exist, or where the computed result can be checked afterwards; **cross-validation** withholds parts of the data during training for post-training verification. **DIN SPEC 13266** additionally provides for a **separate test dataset tested only ONCE, on the final model** — a discipline against overfitting the evaluation itself, and directly transplantable to ADR-010. Test data may be **real** (expensive — requires controlling objects, light sources, train, weather) or **synthetic** (3D-scene imagery, more flexible and voluminous) — but synthetic data **"presumably cannot fully replace"** real data. **(e) EXPLAINABLE AI AS A SAFETY-ARGUMENT INSTRUMENT, AND THE HYBRID PATH — WHICH BEARS ON THE ADR-002 ITEM 6 DECISION OPENED YESTERDAY.** *Erklärbare KI* extracts human-understandable knowledge from ML-learned mappings so people can, in their phrase, **"watch the neural network think"** — judging its **inference rules and thus its reliability**, rather than only its outputs — and can help verify the network's functioning **as early as possible in development**. **ISO 21448** is cited as also proposing XAI to increase trust in a model, and **the EU Commission's expert council is reported as naming transparency a key goal and proposing HYBRID SYSTEMS that combine deep networks' performance with transparency.** DZSF is **participating in DIN SPEC 92001-3 for explainable AI** and preparing a project "**Erklärbare KI für ATO**". **ADR-002 item 6 asks whether the agents must be fully verifiable; this names the middle path — hybrid architectures — and the standards work behind it. ISO 21448, DIN SPEC 13266 and DIN SPEC 92001-3 are all absent from this register.** **(f) THE DATA SCARCITY IS THE PRACTICAL BOTTLENECK, AND DZSF IS FIXING IT IN THE OPEN.** Paraphrased: **hardly any freely available datasets currently exist** with which researchers and developers could build ATO functions or the methods to verify and validate them. Three projects address this — "**Offene Sensordaten ATO**" (DZSF creating such a dataset, **to be published shortly** as of Feb 2023), "**Weiterentwicklung Offene Sensordaten ATO**" (extension with data from other operational environments and further scenarios), and "**Offene Kartendaten ATO**" (adding prepared **digital map data** alongside sensor data). **Together with RailGoerl24/25 from E-2026-08-18-07, DZSF is systematically building the open data substrate for rail AI assurance. Worth tracking: an open, authority-backed dataset is a far better eval baseline than anything vendor-supplied.** **(g) PROJECT REGISTER AS AT FEB 2023** — *Sensorik ATO* (sensors as technical precondition, **report published**) · *ATO Risk* (**risk-acceptance criteria for automated operation**, report in preparation) · *Offene Sensordaten ATO* (report in preparation) · *ATO Sense* (functional requirements for sensors and logic of an ATO unit, in progress) · **ATO Akzeptanz** (*user-group expectations and societal acceptance conditions for automated rail at GoA 3+*, in progress). **ATO Akzeptanz is the one to chase for R10/ADR-002 — societal and user acceptance of automation is the dimension E-2026-08-18-08 and E-2026-08-19-01 both circled, and nobody in this register has evidence on it.** **MOVES: `revise`.** **E-2026-08-18-07 annotated** — the AI-Act-absence finding is scoped to that article and no longer reads as a DZSF position. **ADR-004/R11 gains** the analytical-impossibility statement as the technical basis for the separation. **ADR-010 gains** the D1/D2/D3 data taxonomy, DIN SPEC 13266's once-only test set, and the AI Act Art 10(3) dataset-quality requirement including deliberately adversarial scenarios. **ADR-002 item 6 gains** the hybrid/XAI middle path. **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R11 stays **Proposed — load-bearing** (this strengthens the argument; it does not produce the FFI analysis) · R9/R10 **Accepted (ARB)** · ADR-002/-003 **Accepted (ARB) — NSA concurrence outstanding** · ADR-004/-010 **Proposed**. |

| E-2026-08-19-06 | 2026-08-19 | "**Softwaregestützte Bedrohungsanalyse durch Angriffsgraphen**" / *Software-supported threat analysis using attack graphs* — **Markus Heinrich** (Incyde GmbH) · **Lukas Iffländer** (**DZSF**); **Signal + Draht 114 (05/2022)**, 7 pp, parallel German/English. Output of the DZSF-commissioned project "Prognose Securitybedarf…" | DZSF-funded method paper | Download folder — **this is reference [2] of E-2026-08-19-04, flagged there as missing and now obtained** | **A** | **ADR-007** (primary) · **ADR-012/R14** · **ADR-011** · ADR-010 | **revise** | **TIER A — DZSF-commissioned research with a DZSF staff co-author, publishing a method and open-source tooling.** Heinrich is at **Incyde GmbH**, a commercial security consultancy, so the tool is its own product — but it is **released open source**, and the paper documents *why* it was written rather than promoting a service. Research perspective, not EBA policy (E-2026-08-19-02 disclaimer). **(a) ⚠️ THE METHODOLOGICAL POINT THIS REGISTER HAS BEEN MISSING — SAFETY AND SECURITY DO NOT SHARE A RISK CALCULUS.** Paraphrased: functional safety deals with **hazards**, IT/OT security with the **risk of threats** — and **a threat's occurrence probability cannot be given as a decimal fraction the way a safety hazard's can. The occurrence of a security event (an attack) does NOT follow a stochastic process describable by a probability.** Security therefore uses **semi-quantitative** scales (low/medium/high): **TS 50701** models likelihood through the **exposure** and **vulnerability** of the system under consideration on **levels 1–3**; **DIN VDE V 0831-104**, following **IEC 62443**, requires each threat to be assessed by the attacker's **knowledge, resources and motivation** — which the authors read as indirect semi-quantitative probability modelling. **ADR-012 already says "security ≠ safety but they couple" and asserts ONE GATE FOR CHANGE. This supplies the mathematical reason the coupling is hard: you cannot run a single quantified risk calculus across both. A CSM-RA significance test and a THR/TFFR budget are quantified; a security threat assessment is not and cannot be. The one-gate principle remains right as GOVERNANCE — one decision point, one change record — but the two limbs feeding it produce incommensurable numbers, and ADR-011's change classification must not pretend otherwise.** **(b) THE HONEST FRAMING OF WHAT RISK ANALYSIS IS FOR — WORTH ADOPTING VERBATIM AS A PRINCIPLE.** Paraphrased: **there is no stand-alone "fire-and-forget" product that ensures protection against cyber-attacks, and no one-time integrable solution**; the asset must be **regularly** re-analysed against a **constantly changing** threat situation. **100% protection cannot exist**, because the threat picture changes and countermeasures must be drawn from **limited financial AND HUMAN resources**. **Therefore the task of risk analysis is to determine which risks to MITIGATE and which to ACCEPT**, yielding a **prioritised list of risk-reduction measures** — and **existing countermeasures must be mapped in, or the assessment is not valid.** **This is the same conclusion Katzenbeisser reached at the DZSF conference (E-2026-08-19-03) — cybersecurity cannot be demonstrated once at design and construction for all time — and the same resource constraint that conference named as binding. ADR-012 should carry the accept-vs-mitigate framing explicitly: its action items currently read as a list of things to DO, with no provision for recording what is knowingly accepted.** **(c) THE METHOD, AND WHY IT EXISTS.** Attack graphs derive from **attack trees** — the information-security technique for analysing threats and representing the conditions that must hold for a threat to become a successful attack — with **two deliberate departures from tree properties**: **(1) nodes need not all be connected, so INDEPENDENT attack paths onto one asset can be modelled**; **(2) dropping the "exactly one path between two nodes" rule allows attack sub-steps AND THEIR ASSESSMENTS TO BE REUSED**, where different chainings may lead to different consequences. Assessment is captured in an **attribute vector** which the tool **aggregates into an overall risk, taking account of already-established countermeasures and their risk-reducing effect**. Stated purposes: reduce **effort and error-proneness**, increase **traceability and expressiveness**. **(d) THE TOOLING RATIONALE IS ITSELF EVIDENCE ABOUT THE STATE OF THE FIELD.** The authors surveyed existing software — **both IT-security research tools and commercial or freely available products — and found NONE that fully covers the attack-graph requirements**, explicitly because **previous tools cannot adequately depict the complexity of the railway sector**. They therefore built one and released it open source (`incyde-gmbh/drawio-plugin-attackgraphs`, `INCYDE-GmbH/attackgraphs`). **For ADR-007 item 7 that means the security test surface does not need bespoke tooling procured from a vendor — and for R8/PR13 it is a small but real data point that the rail-specific security tooling market had a gap the public research programme filled openly.** **(e) SECTIONS NOT FULLY MINED IN THIS PASS, RECORDED HONESTLY:** §3 *Threat catalogues and threat mining*, §4 *Risk assessment* (the attribute-vector mechanics), §5 *Countermeasures* and §6 *Conclusion* were read only in outline. **If ADR-007 item 7 is built on this method, §3 and §4 must be read in full first — the threat-catalogue source and the attribute definitions are where the method's assumptions live.** **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-007 item 7** — the method reference now points at the primary method paper rather than at a secondary mention. **ADR-011 gains** the incommensurable-risk-calculus caveat on its change classification. **ADR-012 gains** the explicit mitigate-vs-accept framing. **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R14 **Open** · ADR-007/-010/-011/-012 **Proposed**. SECURITY item → mirrored. |

| E-2026-08-19-07 | 2026-08-19 | "**Vorgehensweise bei der Risikoanalyse Automatisches Fahren**" / *Approach for a Risk Analysis for Automated Train Operation* — **Jens Braband, Siemens Mobility GmbH**; **Signal + Draht 113 (10/2021)**, pp. 25–34, parallel German/English. **The methodology paper of the DZSF-commissioned ATO-RISK project** | Contracted-research methodology paper | Download folder `25-34-braband.pdf` | **A** | **ADR-004/R11** (primary) · **ADR-002/ADR-003** · **ADR-010** · ADR-011 · R9 | **revise** | **TIER A — the methodology of a DZSF-commissioned project, by a recognised authority on rail risk acceptance, published in a peer venue. Not promotional: no product, no architecture, nothing sold.** ⚠️ **INDEPENDENCE NOTE, AND IT IS A REAL ONE THIS TIME.** Braband is **Siemens Mobility**; **Markus Wischy (E-2026-08-15-53, ERJU System Pillar Cyber Security domain lead) is also Siemens Mobility.** **Siemens is therefore embedded in BOTH the European standardisation programme AND the German safety-research programme that this register has been treating as independent institutional sources. That is not misconduct — the expert pool is small and these are the people who know the material — but the register must stop counting ERJU and DZSF outputs as fully independent corroboration where Siemens authorship sits behind both.** Cf. the same effect logged for Benoliel across three affiliations. **(a) ⚠️ THE BOUNDARY CONDITION THAT MATTERS MOST TO THIS ENGAGEMENT — ATO-RISK EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES CYBER SECURITY.** The project's stated constraints: **R1** train movements on normal routes in the **Eisenbahnen des Bundes** network, focus **GoA 3 and GoA 4**; **R2** no solution architectures evaluated and **no safety objectives derived for technical components**; **R3** quantitative results (e.g. **THR**) to match in order of magnitude, or deviations not statistically significant; **R4 — considerations relate to FUNCTIONAL SAFETY per the CENELEC standards; NO other safety aspects, "EXPLICITLY CYBER SECURITY", occupational safety or fire protection, are within scope**; **R5** human performance (sensory perception, information-processing ability) excluded and handled in the parallel **ATO-SENSE** project. **So the risk-acceptance criteria for automated German rail were derived with security deliberately out of scope, and human perception in a different project. E-2026-08-19-06 established that safety and security cannot share a quantified risk calculus; this shows how the German programme handles that in practice — by separating the projects. ADR-012's "one gate for change" must therefore reconcile two workstreams that the national research programme itself keeps apart, and ADR-004's boundary sits exactly on the seam.** **(b) THE POSITION OUR OWN LAYER IS IN, CONFIRMED FROM A THIRD SOURCE.** Paraphrased: introducing automated driving on the federal network **is undoubtedly a significant change within the meaning of the CSM regulation**, at least for the GoA 3/GoA 4 driverless variants — whereas **ATO at GoA 2 can already be regarded as state of the art**, with approved implementations existing, e.g. **Digital Rail at S-Bahn Hamburg**. The CSM process must therefore be followed, and **"an explicit risk analysis will probably be necessary for many of the hazards, as there are NEITHER CODES OF PRACTICE NOR REFERENCE SYSTEMS."** **That is the same CSM-RA §2.1.4 route recorded at E-2026-08-19-02 and written into ADR-004 — and it is precisely where the agentic oversight layer sits. Three independent DZSF-linked sources now converge on it: for a novel rail function with no precedent, explicit risk estimation is the route.** **(c) WHY SEMI-QUANTITATIVE, AND THE METHOD THE REGISTER SHOULD ADOPT.** A semi-quantitative approach was chosen **because there is not enough data available in Germany for a quantitative risk analysis to reliably estimate the numerous required parameters** — demonstrated previously by the risk analysis for radio-based operation (FFB), of comparable scope. The instrument is **DIN VDE V 0831-103**: a German standard since 2014, coordinated by recognised experts including from mass transit, **updated September 2020 to align with the CSM regulation and DIN EN 50129**, and **meeting the CSM regulation's requirements**. Its depicted risk level across CCS applications from **electronic interlocking (ESTW) through level crossings to ETCS corresponds to the safety level accepted on German mainline railways today**, and it was designed and validated against **DIN VDE V 0831-101 as the ONLY semi-quantitative method to date.** **(d) THE RISK SCORE MATRIX, AND WHY ITS SEVERITY SCALE IS DEFENSIBLE.** The RSM's stated advantage: **severity is assessed QUALITATIVELY by accident categories described through typical event types — and those event types were validated against Deutsche Bahn AG's own accident database.** The classifications **err on the side of caution**: not the mean value, but a more conservative yet still credible severity. **An empirically grounded, operator-data-validated severity scale is exactly what an explicit risk analysis for our layer would otherwise have to invent.** **(e) THE FIVE-STEP PROCEDURE — A DIRECTLY REUSABLE TEMPLATE FOR ADR-004 AND ADR-010.** **1. System definition** — identify the functions in scope; characterise the safety objective of the function and its framework conditions; determine **the objects protected by the function and affected by its failure**; identify the relevant **operating scenarios**. **2. Hazard identification** — for each relevant failure type of a function, analyse the potentially resulting effects. **3. Selection of the risk acceptance principle** — **as a rule, EXPLICIT risk analysis for GoA 3/4**; where a code of practice or reference system can exceptionally be used, steps 4–5 are replaced by assessment of that reference system. **4. Determination of severity** — the applicable accident category. **5. Evaluation of the barriers** — determine and evaluate possible barriers per the given tables, **assessing their DEPENDENCE where several barriers exist**. **Step 1 is the system definition ADR-004 still owes (item 1), and step 5's barrier-dependence assessment is the freedom-from-interference question in risk terms.** **(f) A REFERENCE-SYSTEM CAVEAT WORTH REMEMBERING.** Germany's only approved driverless subway, **Nuremberg**, was also evaluated semi-quantitatively — **but that method is "not generally accepted in mainline railways."** Mass-transit systems may nonetheless serve as **reference systems provided the boundary conditions are comparable.** **Relevant to the register's own cross-domain borrowings: a metro precedent is usable, but only with the comparability argument made explicitly — and the method that approved it does not transfer.** **(g) STANDARDS NOW NAMED AND STILL NOT HELD: DIN VDE V 0831-101, -103 and -104.** **-103 is the priority** — it is the only CSM-compliant semi-quantitative method validated against -101, its severity scale is DB-accident-data-validated, and both this paper and E-2026-08-19-02's system-definition template rest on it. **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-004 gains** the five-step CSM-compliant procedure as the template for its outstanding system definition and boundary specification, plus the **barrier-dependence** framing of freedom-from-interference. **ADR-012 gains** the finding that the national ATO risk work excludes security by design. **The DIN VDE V 0831-103 acquisition is escalated to the top of the standards-to-obtain list.** **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R11 stays **Proposed — load-bearing** · R9 **Accepted (ARB)** · ADR-004/-010/-011/-012 **Proposed**. |

Produced under **KI.NRW** and the project **"Zertifizierte KI"** (developing and standardising test criteria, methods and tools for AI systems); www.iais.fraunhofer.de/ki-pruefkatalog | Public-research assessment methodology | Download folder `ausgabe.pdf` — **generic filename, no title metadata; identity established from the cover** | **A** | **ADR-010** (primary) · **ADR-002** · R9/R10 · ADR-003 | **watch** | **TIER A — Fraunhofer IAIS is a public research institute and this is its own published methodology, funded under a state AI-certification programme.** Primary as to the catalogue itself; **not a regulatory instrument and not a standard.** ⚠️⚠️ **READING CAVEAT, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT BOUNDS EVERYTHING BELOW: I read the table of contents, the funders, the executive summary and the STRUCTURE of the Autonomy-and-Control dimension. I did NOT read the 166 pages of substance — the per-dimension risk areas, criteria and measures are the actual content and remain unread. Nothing here should be treated as an assessment of the catalogue's quality, only of its shape and fit.** ⚠️ **AND TWO LIMITS THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE FIT:** **(1) ZERO RAIL CONTENT** — "Bahn", "Eisenbahn" and "rail" appear **0 times** in 166 pages; its worked examples are credit scoring, personnel selection, CV analysis, car-body QA and autonomous driving. **(2) FIVE YEARS OLD AND PRE-AI-ACT** — published **July 2021**, it positions itself against **"der Verordnungsentwurf der Europäischen Kommission"**, i.e. the Commission's **DRAFT** AI Regulation of April 2021, alongside the **Normungsroadmap KI** and the **HLEG on AI** recommendations. **"KI-Verordnung" appears 0 times. Any mapping it offers to AI Act obligations predates the adopted Reg (EU) 2024/1689 by three years and must be treated as stale.** **(a) WHY IT IS WORTH HAVING ANYWAY — ADR-010 IS BLOCKED WITH EVERY METRIC UNDEFINED, AND THIS IS AN OPERATIONALISED SKELETON.** The catalogue's stated purpose is precisely the register's problem: abstract trustworthiness requirements **"müssen konkretisiert und greifbar gemacht werden"** — must be concretised and made tangible. Its assessment chain runs **Schutzbedarfsanalyse (protection-needs analysis) → Risikoanalyse und Zielvorgaben (risk analysis + targets) → Kriterien zur Zielerreichung (criteria for meeting the targets) → Maßnahmen (measures) → Gesamtbewertung per risk area → summary per dimension → cross-dimensional judgement of the application's trustworthiness.** **That is a complete, risk-based evaluation structure of the kind ADR-010 has been unable to specify — and it composes with, rather than competes against, the rail-specific work: DZSF supplies the domain layer (E-2026-08-19-02/-05/-07), this supplies the generic AI-assessment layer. They must be COMPOSED, not substituted.** **(b) SIX TRUSTWORTHINESS DIMENSIONS, AND ONE OF THEM IS LITERALLY THIS ENGAGEMENT'S R9 AND R10:** **Fairness · AUTONOMIE UND KONTROLLE · Transparenz · Verlässlichkeit · Sicherheit · Datenschutz.** The Autonomy-and-Control dimension decomposes into exactly two risk areas: **(5.1) "Angemessene und verantwortungsvolle Gestaltung der AUFGABENVERTEILUNG zwischen Mensch und KI-Anwendung"** — appropriate and responsible design of the **task allocation between human and AI** — and **(5.2) "Sicherstellung der INFORMIERTHEIT und BEFÄHIGUNG von Nutzer*innen und Betroffenen"** — ensuring the **informedness and capability of users and affected persons.** **⚠️ THAT IS A THREE-WAY CONVERGENCE THE REGISTER SHOULD NOTE: Fraunhofer's generic assessment catalogue, Rieth's human-autonomy teaming work for ERA/DZSF (E-2026-08-19-01, the left-over principle and flexible function allocation), and DZSF's ATO position (E-2026-08-19-02, "which basic functions must still be covered by a human") all independently make TASK ALLOCATION BETWEEN HUMAN AND MACHINE the central design question — and 5.2 restates E-2026-08-19-01's requirement that the operator must hold the system's logic, capabilities and limitations. ADR-002's HITL ladder is a task-allocation scheme that has never been assessed as one.** **(c) A STRUCTURAL DEVICE WORTH BORROWING REGARDLESS OF THE REST.** Within each risk area, **measures are decomposed four ways: Daten · KI-Komponente · Einbettung · Maßnahmen für den Betrieb** (data · the AI component · its embedding · operational measures). **That separation of the component from its EMBEDDING and from OPERATIONS is exactly the distinction ADR-004 draws architecturally and ADR-002 draws governance-wise, expressed as an assessment structure — and it gives ADR-010 a place to put controls that are neither model properties nor architecture, which is where oversight-effectiveness and automation-bias measures actually live.** **(d) THE FRAMING INSIGHT, AND IT LANDS ON AN OPEN ADR-002 DECISION.** The executive summary's central claim, paraphrased: **concrete quality criteria depend strongly on the APPLICATION CONTEXT, while the measures available to meet them depend strongly on the AI TECHNOLOGY used** — CV screening and car-body image recognition are not assessed alike. **That is the same axis as ADR-002 item 6 (constrain the agents' implementation class), approached from the assessment side: what you can demonstrate depends on what you built. It also restates, in generic terms, the DZSF "vollständig prüfbar" distinction at E-2026-08-19-02.** The risk illustration used — **severe mispredictions arising from small disturbances in the input data, e.g. pedestrians unrecognised by an autonomous vehicle because of noisy imagery** — is the identical failure class DZSF describes for BF3 perception. **(e) BSI IS REFERENCED 57 TIMES — a live route to check currency.** With ACS membership now in place, whether a post-AI-Act successor or a BSI-endorsed equivalent exists is a cheap question to ask, and it belongs alongside the TR-03183 question already drafted in `project/09-acs-enquiry-2026-08-18.md`. Note also **Fraunhofer appears twice in this register now** — IAIS here, **SIT** as co-author of E-2026-08-19-04 — different institutes, so not a shared-source concern. **MOVES: NO — `watch`, and NO MATRIX REF, deliberately.** A generic, five-year-old, pre-AI-Act catalogue with zero rail content, whose substance I have not read, is **not** matrix-grade for a rail architecture spine — the same discipline applied at E-2026-08-15-55 and -56. **Follow-ups before it can move anything: (i) read §2.3 and the Autonomy-and-Control dimension in full; (ii) establish whether a post-Reg (EU) 2024/1689 edition or successor exists; (iii) if both hold up, propose it to ADR-010 as the generic assessment layer beneath the DZSF rail layer.** **NO STATUS CHANGE:** R9/R10 **Accepted (ARB)** · ADR-002/-003 **Accepted (ARB) — NSA concurrence outstanding** · ADR-010 **Proposed**. |

| E-2026-08-19-09 | 2026-08-19 | "**DIN SPEC 92005:2024-03 — Künstliche Intelligenz: Quantifizierung von Unsicherheiten im Maschinellen Lernen**" / *Artificial Intelligence — Quantification of uncertainties in machine learning*; **DIN Deutsches Institut für Normung**, English text, **46 pp**, published **March 2024** | National specification (DIN SPEC) — **held, read directly** | Download folder `3521675.PDF` — **licensed copy, watermarked `DIN Media / Vpnet Consulting LLC / KdNr.8519157`** | **A** | **ADR-010** (primary) · **ADR-004/R11** · **ADR-002** · R10 · PR5/PR11 · PR6 | **revise** | **TIER A — this is the instrument itself, read first-hand, not a description of it. No vendor, no product, no promotion; issued by the national standards body.** ⚠️ **TIER CAVEAT THAT TRAVELS WITH ALL THREE OF TODAY'S DIN ROWS: a DIN SPEC IS NOT A DIN EN.** It is produced under PAS-type procedural rules by a named author group, **not** the full consensus-committee process of a harmonised standard. It is therefore **tier A as to its own content** but carries **materially lower normative weight**, confers **no presumption of conformity**, and cannot be cited as though it were an EN. ⚠️ **HANDLING: licensed, copyrighted, and personally watermarked. Paraphrase only; the PDFs do not leave the download folder and are not attachments to anything.** Note the licence is held by **Vpnet Consulting LLC**, not Vpnet Cloud Solutions Sdn. Bhd. — a live question now that `00-charter.md` distinguishes the entities. **(a) ⚠️ THE SCOPE EXCLUSION, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT BOUNDS EVERYTHING BELOW.** Clause 1 expressly excludes requirements for **uncertainty criteria necessary for safety functions and health protection** — the worked example is **detection of persons in a hazardous area** — and the exclusion **extends to assistance systems**. **So Germany's AI-uncertainty specification deliberately stops at the edge of the safety-critical case. That is the THIRD German instrument in two days to carve out precisely the intersection this engagement occupies:** ATO-RISK excludes cyber security and human performance (E-2026-08-19-07); the Fraunhofer catalogue holds zero rail content (E-2026-08-19-08); this excludes safety functions. **⚠️ THE PATTERN IS ITSELF THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS ROW: the national AI-assurance layer is being assembled with the safety-critical, human-facing case carved out of every single instrument. Nobody is composing them. That is a gap in the German landscape, not merely in this register — and it is the strongest evidence to date that this engagement's problem is real rather than self-assigned.** **(b) §7.5 SEPARATION OF CONCERNS — THE ADR-004 BOUNDARY, RESTATED AT THE AI LAYER.** Uncertainty-quantification approaches **should follow the separation-of-concerns principle**: the ML model is responsible for producing accurate outputs, while **the uncertainty quantification is INDEPENDENTLY responsible for producing dependable uncertainty estimates**; §7.6 adds that the approach **should be model-agnostic**, i.e. how uncertainty is determined should not depend on the specific model. **⚠️ THIS IS THE REGISTER'S OWN DETECTION PRINCIPLE — "a component that lies about its health cannot be its own alarm" (PR5/PR11, ITU-T Q.752 out-of-band monitoring, E-2026-06-30-03) — published as a requirement for AI. The argument for independent bearer monitoring and the argument for independent uncertainty quantification are the SAME argument at two layers. That is a strong, citable structural alignment and ADR-004 should use it: the silent-failover lesson generalises to the learning components.** **(c) CLAUSE 7 GIVES ADR-010 ITS FIRST CONCRETE, CITABLE REQUIREMENT SET — AND ADR-010 CURRENTLY HAS EVERY METRIC UNDEFINED.** Normative statements, paraphrased: UQ **shall** be designed against a **defined operational design domain** (7.1.6) and **shall** be sensitive to different situations within that ODD (7.2); **should** address all relevant uncertainty sources (7.3) and take account of all relevant factors (7.4); **shall** provide estimates carrying a **statistical confidence** (7.7); **shall be calibrated** to the extent that sufficiently high reliability is ensured (7.8); **shall avoid overconfident uncertainty estimates** (7.9); and the uncertainty itself **shall be interpretable/transparent (7.10) and explainable (7.11)**, with system integration addressed at 7.12. **(d) CALIBRATION IS DEFINED AND MEASURABLE — THIS IS THE PIECE ADR-010 WAS MISSING.** §4.5: a model is **well-calibrated** when its predicted uncertainty distribution matches the actually observed distribution of prediction errors within its ODD, assessed on a **dedicated calibration-validation dataset**. **Expected Calibration Error (ECE)** is named as the measure, with **histogram binning** as a post-hoc correction; for continuous outputs, **quantile / variance / distribution calibration** are distinguished by intended task (distribution calibration being the most restrictive). **ADR-010 can now write "calibrated, ECE-measured on a dedicated dataset, no overconfident estimates, ODD-scoped" where it currently writes nothing.** **(e) RUNTIME MONITORING AND THE UNCERTAINTY TAXONOMY — WHERE THE RESIDUAL BECOMES MEASURABLE.** §5.2: quantified uncertainty **monitored at runtime** to establish whether a decision resting on a model prediction is reliable, with architectural patterns referenced for operation-phase monitoring. Uncertainty decomposes as **aleatoric (data) + epistemic (model)**, or alternatively as **model-fit + input-quality + SCOPE-COMPLIANCE** uncertainty. **⚠️ Scope-compliance uncertainty is the out-of-ODD case — which is precisely DZSF's "an analytical proof excluding errors on UNKNOWN inputs from KNOWN inputs is not possible" (E-2026-08-19-05) given a name and a measurement route. It does not solve that problem, and 92005 excludes safety functions so it does not claim to. But it converts an unquantified hazard into a monitored one, which is the difference ADR-004's argument turns on.** **(f) A TRANSPARENCY DEFINITION WORTH ADOPTING WHOLESALE.** §3.25 decomposes model transparency into **algorithmic transparency + decomposability + simulatability**, and notes explicitly that **a white-box model is not necessarily transparent** — the worked example being a white-box DNN with ~10 million weights over machine-encoded features, which fails all three. **ADR-002 item 6 asks whether the agents must be "fully verifiable"; this replaces that binary with a three-part test that can actually be applied to a candidate implementation.** **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-010 gains** the Clause 7 requirement set and the §4.5 calibration definition as its metric spine (new action item). **ADR-004 gains** §7.5 separation-of-concerns as the AI-layer restatement of its boundary and of PR5/PR11 independent detection. **ADR-002 gains** the §3.25 three-part transparency test against item 6. **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R10 **Accepted (ARB)** · R11 **Proposed — load-bearing** · ADR-004/-010 **Proposed**. |

| E-2026-08-19-10 | 2026-08-19 | "**DIN SPEC 92001-3:2023-08 — Künstliche Intelligenz: Life Cycle Prozesse und Qualitätsanforderungen — Teil 3: Erklärbarkeit**" / *AI — Life Cycle Processes and Quality Requirements — Part 3: Explainability*; **DIN**, English text, **24 pp**, published **August 2023**; normative reference **ISO/IEC 22989** | National specification (DIN SPEC) — **held, read directly** | Download folder `3446955.PDF` — **licensed copy, same watermark** | **A** | **ADR-002** item 6 (primary) · **ADR-010** · **PR4** · R10 · ADR-004 | **revise** | **TIER A — the instrument itself, read first-hand.** Same **DIN SPEC ≠ DIN EN** caveat and same handling restriction as E-2026-08-19-09. ⚠️ **PLUS A SECOND, SELF-DECLARED LIMIT THAT MUST NOT BE GLOSSED: §1 states the document is NOT a requirements specification and provides NO implementation requirements.** It offers a conceptual and procedural basis for *formulating* explainability requirements. **It is therefore something to reason with, never something to conform to or to claim conformity against.** **(a) THIS IS THE STANDARD DZSF IS PARTICIPATING IN — recorded second-hand at E-2026-08-19-05, now held and read.** That second-hand record is confirmed. **(b) THE FRAMING MOVE, AND IT REFRAMES AN OPEN ADR-002 QUESTION.** §3.1/§5.2: **opacity is a RELATION, not a property** — it is appropriate information about the system being unavailable **to a relevant stakeholder**, and a system should be considered opaque **when a stakeholder's information needs are unsatisfied** at a given lifecycle stage. Explainability is likewise stakeholder-relative: a system is explainable **for a particular stakeholder** when explanation methods can satisfy that stakeholder's needs. The document supplies the scaffolding — **twelve stakeholder roles in six categories, seven lifecycle stages per ISO/IEC 22989, and four characteristic interactions: develop · provide · use · evaluate.** **⚠️ CONSEQUENCE FOR ADR-002: "are the agents explainable?" is not a well-formed question, and the register has been asking it that way. The well-formed question is "explainable TO THE SIGNALLER, AT THE MOMENT OF THE ALERT, sufficiently for them to act?" — a different and considerably harder bar than explainable to the developer during validation. The HITL ladder's decision classes are in effect stakeholder × lifecycle-stage pairs, and have never been analysed as such.** **(c) ⚠️ §6.6 "RISKS OF EXPLANATION" — AUTOMATION BIAS AND ITS INVERSE, IN STANDARDS LANGUAGE. THE MOST DIRECTLY USABLE PASSAGE IN THE DOCUMENT, AND IT LANDS ON PR4.** Paraphrased: explanation is neither free nor reliably beneficial. A stakeholder may **reject a CORRECT AI-supported decision** through misinterpreting the explanation — **especially a domain expert who disagrees with the model's learned solution**, because a system's decision path can legitimately deviate from human reasoning. Conversely, misinterpreting an explanation can **support an INCORRECT decision and produce over-reliance on an inadequate system**. Long processing times or over-complex explanations lead to **neglect of the explanations or underuse of the system as a whole**. There may be an explainability/accuracy trade-off, and where reduced performance outweighs the effects of opacity, explanation may not be warranted at all. **⚠️ BOTH FAILURE DIRECTIONS — the expert who overrides correct advice, and the operator who over-trusts wrong advice — are exactly the oversight-effectiveness risk PR4 names, and this register has held no source that framed them as failure modes OF THE EXPLANATION ITSELF rather than of the human. ADR-002's HITL gate and ADR-010's oversight-effectiveness measurement must treat the explanation as a component that can fail, not as the mitigation that makes failure go away.** **(d) §7.3 EXPLANATION QUALITIES — A READY-MADE CRITERION SET FOR ADR-010.** Seven qualities, paraphrased: **explanation documentation** (state the method's applicability and underlying assumptions, verifiable properties and approximation errors, plus a stability analysis where the method has non-deterministic components); **fidelity and accuracy** (the explanation must approximate as precisely as possible what the system actually relied on; where an explanation is used as a surrogate its predictive accuracy must not fall significantly below the model's; **divergence between methods indicates low fidelity**); **stability and consistency** (unintentional input noise must not change the explanation; different methods applied to the same system should agree — the document names the **XAI disagreement problem** and requires comparison metrics); **psychological appropriateness** (**availability bias** and the **mere exposure effect** named explicitly, with mitigations: show prior probabilities; avoid "flash-like" presentation; reduce the total volume of information); **conceptual alignment** (with an acknowledged trade-off against fidelity, since abstraction risks oversimplification); **explanation variety**; **completeness**. **(e) ⚠️ THE FIDELITY ADMISSION — THE SINGLE MOST QUOTE-WORTHY PASSAGE, AND AN UNCOMFORTABLE ONE.** §7.3.2 concedes a **conceptual limitation of ALL explanation methods: fidelity generally cannot be measured against a ground truth, because the system's actual inner logic is exactly what the method is supposed to reveal.** In most real-world applications the true degree of fidelity **may therefore be uncertain**; mathematical theory or benchmark tests on ground-truth synthetic data are offered as partial routes. **This belongs in ADR-004 and in any EBA-facing material: an explanation is not evidence of correctness, and a safety argument that leans on XAI output as assurance leans on something whose own accuracy is unestablished. It REINFORCES the R11 separation rather than weakening it — explainability is not a route to putting learning components inside the vital layer.** **(f) WHEN EXPLANATION IS NEEDED — TWO FACTORS, BOTH POINTING THE SAME WAY FOR RAIL.** §6.5: **reliability** (demonstrably high reliability can reduce the need for explanation) and **stakes** (the cost of errors raises it; medical diagnosis contrasted with retail recommenders). **Rail is maximum-stakes with unestablished reliability for learning components — both factors point at maximum explanation demand, precisely where §7.3.2 says fidelity cannot be verified. That tension is the honest statement of where the agentic oversight layer sits, and it should be stated rather than resolved.** **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-002 gains** the stakeholder-relative reframing of item 6 and the §6.6 risks-of-explanation finding. **ADR-010 gains** the seven §7.3 explanation qualities as criteria and the §6.6 failure directions as oversight-effectiveness measures. **PR4 gains** a source treating explanation as failure-capable. **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R10 **Accepted (ARB)** · ADR-002 **Accepted (ARB) — NSA concurrence outstanding** · ADR-010 **Proposed**. |
