| E-2026-08-19-12 | 2026-08-19 | "**Security Engineering in Safety-critical Railway Signalling**" — **Markus Heinrich**, doctoral dissertation, **Fachbereich Informatik, Technische Universität Darmstadt**; referees **Prof. Stefan Katzenbeisser** and **Prof. Max Mühlhäuser**; submitted 29.10.2020, **defended 10.12.2020**, published on TUprints 2021 (`urn:nbn:de:tuda-tuprints-134847`), **136 pp**, v2.0.0. Constituent chapters previously peer-reviewed at **IEEE ISI 2018**, **Security and Communication Networks 2019**, **SAFECOMP/Springer 2020**, **IEEE VNC 2020** | Doctoral dissertation — peer-reviewed academic research | Download folder `Dissertation_Markus_Heinrich_v2.0.0.pdf` — **CC BY-SA 4.0**, openly licensed | **A** | **ADR-012/R14** (primary) · **ADR-002** item 6 · **ADR-004/R11** · ADR-010 · ADR-007 · R12 · R3/R4 | **revise** | **TIER A — an examined and defended doctoral dissertation whose constituent chapters were separately peer-reviewed in recognised venues. Primary research, not a description of research; no product, no vendor, nothing sold.** ⚠️ **HANDLING — AND IT IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE DIN ROWS: this is CC BY-SA 4.0 and openly hosted on TUprints. It may be QUOTED with attribution and CITED IN PUBLICATION.** Of the German corpus this register leans on, it is one of the few items that can travel into Track A's published output without a licensing question. ⚠️ **THREE LIMITS, STATED BEFORE THE CONTENT.** **(1) It is research, not a standard, not a regulatory instrument and not an operator position** — it proposes and evaluates, it does not bind. **(2) It is from 2020**; its ANN work predates current architectures, and its legal framing cites the NIS Directive and the German IT-Sicherheitsgesetz, i.e. **pre-NIS-2, pre-CRA, pre-AI-Act**. **(3) Author affiliation has since changed** — Heinrich is at **Incyde GmbH** in the later DZSF work (E-2026-08-19-06); at the time of writing he was an academic and this document sells nothing. **Independence note: Christian Schlehuber, co-author of the underlying security-architecture papers, is Deutsche Bahn — so the architecture line is operator-grounded, which is a strength, but it is not independent OF DB.** **(a) ⚠️ CHAPTER 8 IS A PUBLISHED ANSWER TO THE PRINCIPLE BEHIND ADR-012 ACTION 9, AND IT ARRIVES ONE DAY AFTER THAT ITEM WAS WRITTEN.** The register's position (E-2026-08-19-06, and item 9 as drafted) is that **safety and security cannot share a quantified risk calculus** — an attack has no stochastic probability. Item 9 therefore asks how a single change gate adjudicates between two incommensurable bodies of evidence. **Heinrich's methodology answers the composition question by refusing the premise that a common currency is needed: the security control ACTIVELY TRANSFORMS a security incident into a SAFETY HAZARD that the safety layer already knows how to handle.** Paraphrased mechanism: the safe-transmission layer already has a defined threat/error vocabulary — **deletion · corruption · delay · unavailability** (plus insertion, re-sequencing, repetition, masquerade). On detecting an attack, the security control **deliberately expresses its reaction in that vocabulary**: an IPS or secure transmission protocol can **inject a random single-bit error so the safety core's CRC detects "corruption"**, or **drop the message so it appears as accidental "deletion"** in transmission. **"In this way, an attack on the component appears as a hazard to the safety system that it is already able to cope with by design."** The bit-error route is preferred over silent discard **because the message still reaches the safety core, so timestamps, sequence numbers and error counters keep their continuity, and the safety layer's own re-request mechanisms can act.** **⚠️ THE TRANSFERABLE PRINCIPLE, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE IN THIS ROW: you do not reconcile the two calculi — you require the security side to express its output in the safety side's existing, already-certified vocabulary, at the point of detection. The safety layer then reacts with mechanisms that are already in the safety case.** **(b) BUT BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT CLOSE — THIS IS A RUNTIME ANSWER, NOT A CHANGE-GATE ANSWER.** Chapter 8 solves **runtime composition**: how a security control may sit next to a safety core without invalidating it. **ADR-012 item 9 asks a different question — how a security finding and a safety finding are weighed when APPROVING A CHANGE.** The two are related and the principle transfers, but **the dissertation does not supply a change-classification rule and must not be cited as if it did.** Item 9 remains open; what changes is that it now has a **published, in-domain design principle to build on instead of an empty page** — and that principle is available *without* DIN VDE V 0831-103/-104, which are paywalled and unobtainable (see § Open threads). **The scoring scales are still needed for the quantitative half; the architectural half is now answerable.** **(c) ⚠️ CHAPTER 7 IS THE MOST DIRECTLY DECISION-RELEVANT MATERIAL THIS REGISTER HAS FOUND FOR ADR-002 ITEM 6 — AN EMPIRICAL, IN-DOMAIN, RULE-BASED-VERSUS-ANN COMPARISON ON RAILWAY SIGNALLING.** Item 6 asks whether the agents' implementation class must be constrained to fully verifiable methods. This compares both, on the same problem, and states the trade honestly. Paraphrased: **RULE-BASED (RBAD)** — it is **completely traceable how the system reached each individual classification, which enables and simplifies validation of the system, model and results BY DOMAIN EXPERTS**; it needs **no FPR/FNR trade-off**, because the rules partition all possible station configurations into critical and non-critical and the system **raises an alert and prevents the transition before a critical configuration is entered**; its errors are **not intrinsic statistical error** but **configuration mistakes or model incompleteness — both correctable by amending the ruleset**. Its weakness: the model is **known to the attacker**, who can analyse it for evasion, and it deliberately omitted infrequent cases, auxiliary actions and local specifics. **ANN** — decision-making is **generally not traceable, so the system can only be validated against the test dataset**; it is **"unlikely to be correct in all operational situations"**; **FPR and FNR must be traded off against each other and can never both be ruled out**, requiring per-station threshold tuning. Its strength: it detects a **superset** of the rule-based system's attacks — all fall-back cases and local subtleties are implicitly learned — but **at the cost of reduced accuracy**, and **misconfiguration is impossible because the model is built the same way every time**. **⚠️ THE ASYMMETRY ADR-002 SHOULD RECORD: the rule-based system's failures are FIXABLE (amend the rules); the ANN's are IRREDUCIBLE (tune the trade-off, never eliminate it). For a layer whose whole claim is that it can be governed, "our errors are correctable" is a qualitatively different property from "our error rate is tuned" — and this is the first in-domain, quantified statement of that distinction the register holds.** **(d) A TRAINING-DATA CONDITION WITH A NEAT AND CITABLE SOLUTION.** The ANN's model is only sound if the training period was **free of cyberattacks** — otherwise the attack is learned as normality. Two proposed assurances, both usable: **draw the dataset from logs of EARLIER, ANALOGUE signal-box generations, where cyberattacks are excluded by construction**; or **treat the period as benign if no accidents occurred during collection**. **The first is elegant and directly relevant to ADR-010's ground-truth problem (PR8): a pre-digital estate is an attack-free corpus by physics rather than by assumption.** **(e) THE THREE CRITICAL SEMANTIC-ATTACK CLASSES — A READY-MADE TEST SURFACE FOR ADR-007.** Identified as the most critical attacks on railway signalling: **(1) switch a point before or below a train; (2) confuse track occupancy to provoke two trains in the same section; (3) set signals to bypass protection of the following section.** Both detectors were validated against all three, the ANN via a **purpose-built artificial attack dataset**. **ADR-007's undefined security test surface (item 7, added 2026-08-15 and still empty) now has three named, in-domain, published attack classes to be built against — and a demonstrated method for generating the adversarial dataset.** **(f) ⚠️ THE AVAILABILITY COST, WHICH CUTS AGAINST R3/R4 AND MUST NOT BE SKIPPED.** An IPS with a **false-positive rate greater than zero drops legitimate messages**, and the whole method works by making security reactions look like transmission faults. **A security control that "fails safe" therefore consumes availability by design — and this register's R4 exists precisely because the estate is provably fail-SAFE and not yet fail-SOFT. Chapter 8's elegance is bought with exactly the currency R3/R4 are short of. Any adoption must state that trade rather than inherit the method's framing, in which reduced availability is an acceptable outcome.** **(g) SCOPE EXCLUSIONS, FOR THE FOURTH TIME IN THREE DAYS.** Chapter 8 places **secure update out of scope** (a maintenance-phase concern assumed supervised by a technician) and **user authentication/authorisation out of scope** (occurring under human supervision). **⚠️ Secure update is ADR-012's central trade — the CRA update duty against railway change-control. So the one published methodology that composes security with safety at runtime explicitly excludes the lifecycle problem this register calls "one gate for change". The pattern logged at E-2026-08-19-09 holds: every instrument excludes the seam.** **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-012 gains** the incident-to-hazard transformation as the design principle beneath action 9, with the runtime/change-gate distinction stated so it is not over-claimed. **ADR-002 item 6 gains** the traceable-versus-learned comparison and the correctable-versus-irreducible asymmetry. **ADR-007 gains** the three semantic-attack classes as its security test surface. **ADR-010 gains** the attack-free-training-corpus route to ground truth. **ADR-004 gains** the observation that a security control expressing itself only in the safe direction is architecturally distinct from actuation. **NO STATUS FLIPS — and none is warranted: R3 Strengthened post-incident — open · R4 Open · R11 Proposed — load-bearing · R12 Proposed · R14 Open. Research support is not test evidence, and ADR-012 remains blocked on its own action items.** |

| E-2026-08-19-13 | 2026-08-19 | "**Sind Eisenbahn- und ÖPNV-Sektor fit für die heutigen Cybersecurity-Herausforderungen?**" / *Is the railway and public transport sector fit for today's cybersecurity challenges?* — **Lukas Iffländer (DZSF)** · **Dr. Kristin Mühl (DZSF, Referentin Human Factors)** · **MBA Michael Nord (IABG, Programm-Manager und zert. CISO)**; **ETR — Eisenbahntechnische Rundschau, November 2022, Nr. 11**, 6 pp, German. **Reports the DZSF-commissioned study "Studie Security und geplanter Technologieeinsatz"** (Nord, Leppla, Möller, Krause, Lenski, Czerkewski; DZSF 2022, **doi 10.48755/dzsf.220011.01**), executed with **IABG · 3DSE Management Consultants · Fraunhofer AISEC · IFB Institut für Bahntechnik** | Contracted-research results reported by their own authors in a professional venue | Download folder `2022-05_Fachartikel_ETR_Cybersecurity.pdf` — **© DVV Media Group; the PDF carries an explicit indefinite homepage-publication grant to DZSF and IABG**, i.e. it is redistributed by DZSF itself | **A** | **R12** (primary) · **ADR-012/R14** · **ADR-010** · **ADR-007** · R8/PR13 · PR14 · R3/R4 | **revise** | **TIER A, ON THE ESTABLISHED PRECEDENT AND NOT ON THE VENUE.** ETR is a **trade journal** and by the bare tier definition that reads **C**. It is not C here for the same reason the Signal+Draht rows are not (E-2026-08-19-06, -07): **this is not journalism about someone's research — it is the researchers reporting their own DZSF-commissioned study, two of the three authors being DZSF staff and the third the contractor's certified CISO.** The venue is professional rather than academic; the *content* is primary. ⚠️ **BUT THE PRIMARY ARTEFACT IS THE FULL REPORT, AND WE DO NOT HOLD IT.** This is a **6-page summary** of `doi 10.48755/dzsf.220011.01`; the methodology detail, the instrument and the full data sit in the report. **Everything below is therefore the authors' own summary of their own study — strong, but one step from source. Obtaining the DZSF report is a follow-up and, unlike the DIN VDE texts, DZSF publications are ordinarily free.** ⚠️ **AND THE STUDY'S OWN LIMIT, STATED BY ITS AUTHORS AND NOT TO BE SOFTENED: 715 companies were invited, 60 complete responses were returned (~8 %), 12 interviews. The authors state plainly that the response rate DID NOT REACH the target of covering at least one tenth of each subsector. For the EIU subsector the figures below rest on ELEVEN responses out of 116 invited. Treat the direction as evidenced and the precise values as indicative.** **(a) ⚠️ THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS MOST TO THIS ENGAGEMENT — THE INFRASTRUCTURE MANAGERS ARE THE WEAKEST SUBSECTOR, AND THEY ARE WEAKEST EXACTLY WHERE R12 SAYS THEY ARE.** Maturity was scored on the **NIST CSF** five functions against a **0–5 scale** (0 = no, 3 = fully implemented and documented, 5 = subject to continuous improvement). Sector totals: **overall mean 1.96**, best discipline **Recover 2.36**, worst **Respond 1.58**. **Eisenbahninfrastrukturunternehmen (EIU) — the infrastructure managers, i.e. the party that would own the estate an FRMCS oversight layer rides on — score CONSISTENTLY BELOW the sector mean on every function: Identify 1.01 · Protect 1.24 · DETECT 1.03 · RESPOND 0.69 · Recover 1.63 · Total 1.15** (±CI as published). By contrast the operating companies (EVU) sit at **Total 2.10** and the vehicle manufacturers above sector level throughout. **⚠️ DETECT 1.03 AND RESPOND 0.69 ARE THE EMPIRICAL FORM OF R12. The register has carried R12 — the awareness/detection gap — on three independent qualitative confirmations and it has never moved. This is the fourth, it is QUANTIFIED, it is the safety authority's own research centre, and it is worse than the register has been assuming: on a 0–5 scale where 1 means "no, but a plan exists", the infrastructure managers' ability to DETECT sits at 1.0 and to RESPOND at 0.7. The 23-June outage was a silent fault nobody detected. This says that is not an anomaly of one operator on one night — it is the sector's measured position.** **(b) THE 0–5 MATURITY INSTRUMENT IS ITSELF USABLE, AND ADR-010 SHOULD TAKE IT.** The scale is published in the article: **0 no · 1 no but planned · 2 yes but partially implemented · 3 yes, fully implemented and documented · 4 yes, and implementation is continuously checked for effectiveness · 5 yes, and implementation is subject to continuous improvement.** **Two reasons to adopt it rather than invent one: (i) it makes the oversight layer's security posture reportable ON THE SAME SCALE the German sector is already measured against, so a claim becomes comparable instead of self-referential; (ii) levels 4 and 5 — "checked for effectiveness" and "continuously improved" — are exactly the distinction ADR-010 keeps needing between HAVING a control and EVIDENCING that it works.** Note also that the study **asked separately about OT and IT where a company distinguishes them** — a split ADR-012 makes architecturally and has never made measurably. **(c) THE SWOT FINDINGS THAT LAND ON R8/PR13 AND PR14 — SUPPLIER DEPENDENCE, IN THE SECTOR'S OWN WORDS.** Recorded weaknesses, paraphrased: **high dependence on supplier firms for the technical standards of procurable hard- and software — "the standard offered is not always the current standard"**; **dependence on manufacturers to set up IT and in some cases even to restore backups**; **manufacturers withdrawing support and updates for older products**; **little support from authorities and politics** for measures to raise cybersecurity; **lacking management and staff awareness**. Risks include **blanket rules across differing rail sectors and use cases hindering companies through lack of individuality and practicability**, **the financial benefit of security investment being underestimated**, **IT skills shortage against high salary expectations**, and **a widening technological gap for want of funding**. **⚠️ "Dependence on the manufacturer to restore a backup" is PR13 (proprietary opacity / vendor-fix dependency) stated by the operators themselves, and it is a sharper formulation than the register's own: it is not merely that the vendor holds the fix, it is that the operator cannot execute its OWN RECOVERY unaided. Read against the 23-June ~90 minutes of manual recovery, that is the same dependency with a name.** **"The standard offered is not always the current standard" is the procurement gate at ADR-012 action 2 justified from the demand side, and it belongs in the CRA bid-condition argument.** **(d) A SIZE EFFECT WITH A DIRECT CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MIGRATION.** Maturity correlates with company size (**Spearman r = .42**, characterised as a medium relationship): **not one micro-enterprise reaches a mean of 2.0**; the median stays **below 1** in the next size band; only above **50 FTE** does the median rise, and only companies above **10,000 FTE** reach 5.0 at all. **⚠️ This is R13 and ADR-009 seen from the security side. The FRMCS migration depends on the whole estate — including the NE-Bahnen and small EVU — and the smallest operators are measurably the least able to secure what they will be asked to retrofit. A migration plan that assumes uniform security capability across the sector is assuming something this study measured and disproved.** **(e) THE STARTING POSITION, HONESTLY STATED BY THE AUTHORS.** A literature search returned little; the most concrete prior work is **ENISA's 2020 Railway Cybersecurity report**, which the authors judge **only limitedly representative with 41 companies across all of Europe and insufficiently meaningful for the German sector**. **That is a useful independent judgement on a source class this register also uses — and it is the reason this study exists.** Attacks to date are noted as having struck predominantly **non-safety-critical systems** (2017 WannaCry on ticket machines and passenger displays; January 2022 on Belarusian rail, primarily the **disposition system**, where the attackers explicitly stated they did not want to endanger travellers), with disruptions in the Netherlands and Poland officially attributed to non-cyber causes. **The pattern — the disposition/optimisation layer attacked, the vital layer not — is precisely the two-domain split ADR-004 draws, observed in the wild.** **(f) TWO NAMES THE ENGAGEMENT NEEDS, AND ONE OF THEM RESOLVES AN OPEN QUESTION.** **Dr. Kristin Mühl is DZSF's *Referentin Human Factors* (muehlk@dzsf.bund.de)** — corroborating the "DZSF Human Factors lead" recorded at E-2026-08-18-08 and **naming the intended addressee of the findings-sharing letter** (`project/08-eba-consultation-2026-08-18.md`, check 5). **Lukas Iffländer (ifflaenderl@dzsf.bund.de)** is DZSF's security-research contact and co-author of the attack-graph work at E-2026-08-19-06. ⚠️ **Both are 2022 attributions and must still be checked for currency before anything is sent — do not treat a four-year-old byline as a current role.** **MOVES: `revise`.** **R12 gains its first quantified, tier-A, authority-commissioned evidence** — Detect 1.03 / Respond 0.69 among infrastructure managers. **ADR-010 gains** the 0–5 NIST CSF maturity instrument and the OT/IT measurement split. **ADR-012 gains** the demand-side justification for its procurement gate and the operator-stated recovery dependency. **ADR-007 gains** the finding that the sector's weakest function is *Respond*, which its test surfaces should therefore exercise hardest. **ADR-009/R13 gains** the size-versus-capability correlation. **PROPOSED STATUS CHANGE — R12 only, and it is a characterisation rather than a ratification: `Proposed` → `Proposed — load-bearing`, matching R11's existing form, on the ground that the gap R12 exists to close is now measured rather than asserted. NO OTHER STATUS FLIPS: R3 Strengthened post-incident — open · R4 Open · R8/R13/R14 unchanged · ADR-007/-009/-010/-012 Proposed. A maturity survey is not test evidence and ratifies nothing.** |

| E-2026-08-20-02 | 2026-08-20 | "**Tele-Tf: Ein neues Berufsbild entsteht**" / *Tele-Tf: a new occupational profile is emerging* — **Birte Thomas-Friedrich M.Sc.** and **Dipl.-Ing. Stefanie Schöne** (both **DLR, Institut für Verkehrssystemtechnik**) · **Dr. Kristin Mühl** (**DZSF**, Wissenschaftliche Referentin Human Factors); **ETR — Eisenbahntechnische Rundschau, November 2024, Nr. 11**, 5 pp, German. Reports the **DZSF-commissioned project "Teleoperation ATO"** (DZSF beim Eisenbahn-Bundesamt; executed by **DLR-Institut für Verkehrssystemtechnik**; full title *"Teleoperation ATO — Rahmenbedingungen und menschzentrierte Gestaltung der Teleoperation als Ergänzung für den automatisierten Bahnbetrieb"*) ⚠️ **RUNTIME CORRECTED AT SOURCE 2026-08-20:** the article states **March 2023 – February 2025**; **the DLR project page now gives March 2023 – SEPTEMBER 2025**, i.e. **the project ran roughly seven months beyond the schedule printed in the article.** Both are accurate at their date; the article's figure is superseded. **Worth noting for how the register reads project dates generally: a runtime printed in a mid-project article is a plan, not an outcome.** | Contracted-research project reported by its own authors in a professional venue | Download folder `2024-11-Fachartikel_ETR_Tele-Tf.pdf` — **"Beleg-E-Paper", © DVV Media Group; republication permitted indefinitely only on the AUTHORS' own company inter/intranet — not ours. Paraphrase, do not redistribute** | **A** | **ADR-002/R10** (primary — action item 8) · **ADR-010/PR4** · **ADR-004/R11** · **R3/R4** · ADR-009 · R12 | **revise** | **TIER A on the established precedent** (E-2026-08-19-06, -07, -13): researchers reporting their own DZSF-commissioned project, with the DZSF human-factors lead as co-author. Trade venue, primary content. ⚠️ **THREE LIMITS. (1) INTERIM, NOT FINAL — the project ran to February 2025 and this was published November 2024; the article says the validated occupational profile was still to be developed in a user-centred process. (2) The full requirements catalogue is NOT in the article and is not held — the authors state a complete presentation would exceed the article's scope. (3) It is about the OCCUPATIONAL PROFILE, not about bearers or architecture; the architectural consequences at (a) are largely OUR inference from what it states, and are marked as such.** **(a) ⚠️ IT ANSWERS ADR-002 ACTION ITEM 8 — OPENED THIS MORNING — AND GIVES THE UNCOMFORTABLE ANSWER.** Item 8 asked whether the ladder's class-4 human is defined as locally present, or whether remote command is in scope. **The German research programme has already chosen: teleoperation is described as essential specifically AS THE FALLBACK LEVEL (*Rückfallebene*) for the ATO system.** The Tele-Tf is a specially trained professional who, when needed, **intervenes from a central control centre using modern communications and control systems to steer trains safely and take complex decisions**; teleoperation is foreseen in European ATO concepts, the **Betuwe route** named as an example, to complement the technology and resolve problems in exceptional situations. Beyond the fallback level, remote operation is also envisaged for **shunting** and for **short sections not equipped for highly automated running**. **⚠️ THE CONSEQUENCE, NOW EVIDENCED RATHER THAN INFERRED: if the fallback level is a human at the far end of a communications link, THE FALLBACK DEPENDS ON THE BEARER. The article raises the link itself as an open design parameter in its own terms — whether the Tele-Tf's communication with other actors runs ENTIRELY ORALLY OVER ZUGFUNK or over digital channels is named as an unresolved question that materially shapes the job. So ADR-002's class-4 "human-in-command" and ADR-001's bearer are NOT INDEPENDENT: a bearer failure of the 23-June class removes the advisory layer AND the fallback human together, leaving the estate with neither. Option (b) at item 8 is the one the sector is actually pursuing; ADR-002 should take it and add a bearer-availability precondition per class, with a defined behaviour for loss of command connectivity.** **(b) A NAMED REGULATORY TEMPLATE — AND IT COMES FROM ROAD LAW.** The authors point to the **StVG amendment on autonomous driving** as an orientation for regulating teleoperation: within a **defined operating area** the automated vehicle **need not be permanently monitored by a human**; on a problem the vehicle **puts itself into a RISK-MINIMAL STATE**, and a **technische Aufsicht** (technical supervision) then either **proposes the manoeuvre by teleoperation or steers directly**. ⚠️ **Apply the register's own cross-domain caution (E-2026-08-19-07, the Nuremberg metro caveat): a road-law pattern is usable only with the comparability argument made explicitly.** **But the STRUCTURE — bounded operating domain · automatic entry to a risk-minimal state · a named human supervisory function that may PROPOSE or TAKE CONTROL — is the closest thing to a legal template for what ADR-002 describes, and the register held nothing comparable. Note also what rail gets for free: its risk-minimal state already exists and is STANDSTILL ("a standing train is a safe train", E-2026-08-19-01) — the hardest part of the road pattern is the part rail has had since the beginning.** **(c) ⚠️ THE OVERSIGHT-CAPACITY PROBLEM, IN DOMAIN, FROM THE SAFETY AUTHORITY'S OWN RESEARCH CENTRE — AND IT IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE THE REGISTER HOLDS FOR PR4.** One Tele-Tf is expected to handle **several trains**, including **prioritising fault reports**; an explicit scenario is **multiple simultaneous takeover requests that cannot be worked in parallel**, requiring prioritisation and **handing tasks off to others**. The workload profile: predominantly **underload from passive monitoring, punctuated by short phases of extremely high demand** — which the authors tie directly to **performance and therefore safety losses**, as well as job dissatisfaction and effects on mental and physical health. Design responses named: **time-bound the monitoring tasks**; issue the **takeover request as early as possible** to allow preparation; have the request **carry the situation detail, the expected handling duration, the criticality and the priority**; **finish one train before taking the next**, to cut cognitive switching cost and **the risk of confusing one train with another**; and offer **job-related secondary tasks** against boredom. **⚠️ ADR-002 ASSIGNS A NAMED HUMAN ROLE PER DECISION CLASS AND HAS NEVER ASKED HOW MANY DECISIONS THAT HUMAN CAN HOLD AT ONCE. This supplies the question and several of the answers, in domain, and it is directly usable as ADR-010 oversight-effectiveness measurement rather than as background.** **(d) TRANSPARENCY STATED AS AN OPERATOR TASK, AND POINTING AT THE SYSTEM.** At a teleoperation workstation, **understanding the automated system becomes one of the most important tasks of the human operators**, and **transparency in the automated system should be present in order to create trust in it.** **Corroborates E-2026-08-19-01 and DIN SPEC 92001-3's stakeholder-relative explainability — and note the direction of the obligation: it falls on the SYSTEM to be holdable, not on the human to try harder. That is the right framing for ADR-002's item 6 rule and for ADR-010's explanation-quality criteria.** **(e) MINIMUM VERSUS BEST CASE — A HARD OPERATIONAL EDGE FOR R4.** Two technical bounds were compared. **With minimal equipment, in an impact or a train-internal fault the Tele-Tf can only act if there is staff on board** (a *Zugbegleiter* or "Zugbegleiter-Plus") able to resolve the situation jointly; **otherwise a recovery/repair team must be dispatched.** In the assumed **Best Case**, supported by diagnostic systems, the Tele-Tf could partly continue to steer even **without staff on site**. **⚠️ The difference between a minutes-long supervised degraded mode and dispatching a team is therefore a question of ON-BOARD DIAGNOSTICS AND EQUIPMENT — not of the remote operator's skill. That is R4 (fail-soft) expressed as a procurement and fitment decision, and it belongs in ADR-009's retrofit pattern.** **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-002 item 8 gains the sector's answer** — remote command is in scope because teleoperation IS the designed fallback; the item stays open because the decision remains ours, but it is no longer open on the facts. **ADR-010 gains** the takeover-request design requirements and the concurrent-load scenario as oversight-effectiveness measures. **ADR-004 gains** the note that a remote command path crosses the boundary differently from a local one. **ADR-009/R4 gains** the on-board-diagnostics dependency. **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R3 **Strengthened post-incident — open** · R4 **Open** · R10 **Accepted (ARB)** · R11 **Proposed — load-bearing** · R12 **Proposed — load-bearing** · ADR-002 **Accepted (ARB) — settled internally** · ADR-004/-009/-010 **Proposed**. |

| E-2026-08-20-03 | 2026-08-20 | **DLR project page — "HEiDi" = *Hochautomatisierte Eisenbahn dank digitalem Zwilling*** (highly automated railway by means of a digital twin). **DLR-Institut für Verkehrssystemtechnik** (coordinator) with **IKADO GmbH**; funded by the **Ministry for Economic Affairs, Industry, Climate Protection and Energy of North Rhine-Westphalia via EFRE**, **€1.8 m**; **runtime January 2026 – December 2028**. Builds a **digital twin of the Wegberg-Wildenrath test centre** including vehicle and sensor models | Research-institute project page, read at source | `https://www.dlr.de/de/ts/forschung-und-transfer/projekte/projekt-heidi` — **read 2026-08-20 after the sandbox egress rule was added; publicly accessible, no licence restriction** | **A** | ADR-007 (primary) · ADR-010/PR8 · ADR-009/R13 · R11 | **watch** | **TIER A as to the project's existence, scope, funding, partners and dates — this is the performing institute's own page.** ⚠️ **BUT A PROJECT PAGE STATES INTENTIONS, NOT RESULTS, AND THIS PROJECT HAS NONE YET: it began January 2026 and runs to December 2028. Nothing here is a finding. It is logged so the register knows the work exists and can return to it, not because it establishes anything.** ⚠️ **NOTE ALSO WHAT IT IS NOT: unlike every other DLR/DZSF item logged this week, HEiDi is NOT DZSF-commissioned — it is a North Rhine-Westphalia state project under EFRE. It therefore sits outside the federal safety-research programme this register has been tracking, and should not be read as part of it.** **(a) WHY IT IS WORTH WATCHING AT ALL — IT TOUCHES THE TWO THINGS ADR-007 AND ADR-010 CANNOT CURRENTLY SUPPLY.** The stated purpose is to let **individual sensors and sensor systems be developed faster, more economically and more flexibly**, by combining **simulation experiments with real testing at the physical test centre**, integrating IKADO's shunting assistant into DLR simulation, and publishing **open source** so others can build on it. The stated deliverable is a **tool chain and open-source digital-twin platform for the development AND APPROVAL of sensors and autonomous systems.** **⚠️ "Approval" is the word that matters. ADR-007's test surfaces are undefined and ADR-010 has a standing ground-truth problem (PR8); a publicly available digital twin of a real test centre, built expressly with approval processes in view, is a candidate source of both — synthetic scenarios that can be replayed, and a reference environment that is not our own invention.** **(b) THE CAUTION THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH IT, AND THE REGISTER ALREADY HOLDS THE ARGUMENT.** A digital twin is a **model**, and evidence generated inside a model is evidence about the model until its fidelity to the real system is argued. **DIN SPEC 92005 (E-2026-08-19-09) names exactly this as scope-compliance uncertainty — the out-of-ODD case — and DZSF (E-2026-08-19-05) states that for ML-based perception an analytical proof excluding errors on unknown inputs is not available in principle. A simulator cannot supply the inputs nobody thought of; that is the same limit in a different costume.** **So: usable for coverage, replay and cheap iteration; not usable, on its own, as the completeness argument ADR-010 item 5 needs.** **(c) A SMALLER POINT WITH REAL PROGRAMME RELEVANCE.** Wegberg-Wildenrath is a working rail test centre, and the project's economic argument is that physical testing is slow and expensive. **ADR-009/R13 carries approval throughput (*Serienzulassung*, Umbaucluster) as a named external dependency on the retrofit programme. If simulation-assisted approval matures, it bears directly on that bottleneck — but on a 2028 horizon, which is beyond the point at which the retrofit decisions must already be taken.** **NO DECISION MOVED — because it is plan-not-outcome:** a project that has produced nothing yet cannot change a decision, and logging intentions as though they were findings is precisely the failure this register's action column exists to prevent. **Revisit when deliverables appear — the open-source commitment means they should be inspectable without a licence or a paywall, which is more than can be said for most of what this register wants.** **NO STATUS CHANGE:** R11 **Proposed — load-bearing** · R13 unchanged · ADR-007/-009/-010 **Proposed**. |

Named below: **ATO-Sense · ForTeS · STREAMLINE · HMI4Rail**, plus the four carried in their own rows (-03 HEiDi, -05 RemODtrAIn, -06 FASaN, -07 ATO-Einsatzszenarien/KI-Systeme) | Research-institute project register, read at source | `https://www.dlr.de/de/ts/forschung-und-transfer/projekte` + per-project pages, read **2026-08-20** after the sandbox egress rule was added. Where a project is still running, nothing it promises is evidence. Each row below is logged so the register knows the work exists and can return to it.** **(a) ⚠️⚠️ THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST, AND IT IS ABOUT THIS REGISTER'S OWN SOURCES: SIEMENS NOW SITS IN A FOURTH INDEPENDENT-LOOKING PLACE.** Recorded at E-2026-08-19-07: **Braband (Siemens Mobility)** authored the DZSF ATO-RISK methodology while **Wischy (Siemens Mobility)** leads the ERJU System Pillar cyber domain — two streams the register had been treating as independent. The survey adds two more: **Siemens is a named partner in ATO-Sense** (the DZSF human-performance baseline project) **and Siemens Mobility GmbH COORDINATES RemODtrAIn**, the €40 m national remote-train-operation programme (row -05). **⚠️ So the same supplier sits behind the European standardisation programme, the national safety-research methodology, the human-performance baseline, AND the demonstrator that will produce the reference architecture. That is not misconduct — the expert pool is small and these are the people who know the material — but the consequence for this register is now unavoidable: ERJU, DZSF and the national demonstrator programme CANNOT be counted as mutually corroborating where Siemens authorship or coordination sits behind all of them. Corroboration counted four times is corroboration once. This bears directly on R8/PR7/PR13 (vendor concentration) in a form the register had only ever framed commercially: the concentration is not merely in supply, it is in the EVIDENCE BASE ITSELF.** **(b) ATO-SENSE — THE DANGLING REFERENCE AT E-2026-08-19-07 IS NOW RESOLVED.** ATO-RISK excluded human performance and referred it to a parallel project; that project is **ATO-Sense — Funktionale Anforderungen an Sensorik und Logik einer ATO-Einheit**. Coordinator **TU Berlin, Fachgebiet Bahnbetrieb und Infrastruktur**; partners **DB Systemtechnik · DLR-TS · Siemens**; client **DZSF**; runtime **01/2021 – 10/2023**. Method: **two simulator studies — one at TU Berlin BBI, one in the DLR RailSiTe® train-driver simulator — experimentally measuring the VISUAL PERCEPTION PERFORMANCE of train drivers under varying conditions**, in order to determine how capable the technical system must be. **⚠️ THIS IS WHERE THE HUMAN BASELINE COMES FROM. E-2026-08-18-07 recorded that DZSF proposes the CSM-RA §2.4 reference-system route for AI perception — benchmarking against quantified human performance. ATO-Sense is the measurement behind that benchmark, and the register now knows its method (simulator, not field) and its scope (visual perception only). A reference system is only as good as the study that quantified it; the register should hold that study before leaning on the route.** **(c) ForTeS — R8's ANTI-LOCK-IN ARGUMENT HAS A TECHNICAL INSTRUMENT, AND IT IS DZSF-FUNDED.** Client **DZSF**, runtime **05/2025 – 04/2027**. Problem stated: many manufacturers now offer interlocking subsystems, but infrastructure managers still cannot practically **mix subsystems from different manufacturers in one interlocking**, because interoperability and safe function of the assembled interlocking must be demonstrated — tasks that formerly sat with the single manufacturer of the whole interlocking. Two-step approach: **formal verification that the SPECIFICATION implies the required interoperability and safety properties**, then **highly automatable conformance testing of an implementation against that specification**, based on the **certification tests published by the EULYNX consortium** (spec published by EULYNX / Europe's Rail System Pillar). **⚠️ The register has argued unbundling (R8/PR13) commercially — separable RAN/core/MCX/dispatcher lots. ForTeS is the same argument made TECHNICALLY, and it names the missing mechanism: multi-vendor assembly is blocked not by procurement but by the absence of a conformance-demonstration route. That belongs in ADR-012's procurement gate and in ADR-001's vendor strategy.** **(d) STREAMLINE — THE APPROVAL BOTTLENECK QUANTIFIED, WITH A NAMED BEST PRACTICE.** Client **Deutsche Maschinentechnische Gesellschaft (DMG)**; partners **DLR-TS** and **IKEM**. Identifies bottlenecks in **cross-border ETCS vehicle authorisation**, assessing all sub-processes — **test → certification/type examination → operating licence** — with legal frameworks, institutional roles and responsibilities across European stakeholders. **The Swiss model is taken as best practice and as the basis for a realistic target process duration: the Swiss approval procedure is clearly defined, roles and rights are proven, and the process is "planbar, deterministisch, kalkulierbar" — planable, deterministic, calculable — and therefore permits viable business models for operators.** **⚠️ ADR-009 carries EBA *Serienzulassung* reform and approval throughput as a named EXTERNAL dependency of the retrofit programme (R13), with no benchmark. This supplies one: the deficiency is not that approval is strict but that its DURATION IS NOT PREDICTABLE, and predictability — not leniency — is what makes a retrofit business case financeable. That reframing should go into ADR-009.** **(e) HMI4Rail — AND A COMPLIANCE QUESTION THIS REGISTER IS OBLIGED TO ASK.** Coordinator **TU Chemnitz**, with DLR-TS and others; client **BMBF**, funded under **WIR! – Smart Rail Connectivity Campus**; runtime **01/2023 – 12/2025**. Develops a **modular, miniaturised, textile-integrated sensor system** combining **respiration rate, heart rate, metabolic parameters and movement** to reliably capture the **current performance and health state of train drivers**, with a **virtual development environment** for automated-operation assistance systems so future systems can be pre-tested virtually and real test runs reduced. **The virtual-environment half is directly useful to ADR-007 and ADR-010** — a validated simulation environment cross-checked against a real test track (SRCC). **⚠️ THE HALF THAT NEEDS CHECKING, AND IT IS NOT AN ACCUSATION: continuous physiological inference of a worker's performance and health state sits close to Reg (EU) 2024/1689 Art 5(1)(f), which prohibits AI systems inferring emotions in the WORKPLACE, subject to an exception for medical or SAFETY reasons. A rail safety application may well fall squarely inside that exception — and the AI Act post-dates the project's start. THE REGISTER MUST NOT ASSERT THAT IT BITES. But ADR-003's entire method is running the Art 6(1) test rather than assuming an answer, and the same discipline applies here: if this engagement ever contemplates operator-state sensing as an oversight-effectiveness measure (ADR-010 item 2), the Art 5 question must be answered FIRST, because a prohibited practice is not a risk to be managed — it is a bar.** **MOVES: `revise`.** **R8/PR13 gains** the finding that vendor concentration extends into the evidence base, not only into supply. **ADR-009/R13 gains** the predictability-not-leniency reframing and the Swiss benchmark. **ADR-012 action 2 gains** ForTeS as the technical route to multi-vendor conformance. **ADR-010 gains** an Art 5(1)(f) precondition on any operator-state sensing. **The ATO-Sense method is recorded against the §2.4 reference-system route.** **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R8, R11, R13 unchanged · ADR-001/-007/-009/-010/-012 unchanged. |

Funder **Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und Energie**. **Project volume €40 m. Runtime 10/2025 – 09/2028** | National demonstrator programme — project page read at source | `https://www.dlr.de/de/ts/forschung-und-transfer/projekte/remodtrain`, read 2026-08-20 | **A** | **ADR-002/R10 — action item 8** (primary) · **ADR-004/R11** · **R3/R4** · ADR-009/R13 · R8/PR13 · ADR-007 | **revise** | **TIER A as to the programme's existence, scope, funding, partners and dates** — a project page of a named participating institute. ⚠️ **PLAN, NOT OUTCOME, AND EARLY: it began October 2025 and runs to September 2028. It has produced nothing yet, and NOTHING BELOW IS A RESULT. What it establishes is that the work is FUNDED, STAFFED AND UNDER WAY — which is itself the decision-relevant fact.** **(a) ⚠️ IT SETTLES ADR-002 ACTION ITEM 8 ON THE FACTS, ONE DAY AFTER THAT ITEM WAS OPENED.** Item 8 asked whether the ladder's class-4 human is defined as locally present, or whether **remote command is in scope**. Stated goal: **the creation of a safety-oriented, modular system and safety architecture in a building-block system (*Baukasten*) for remote train operation, subsequently VALIDATED IN REAL OPERATION** — first at the **ICE works Köln-Nippes with an ICE 4**, then at the **Smart Rail Connectivity Campus Annaberg-Buchholz with a Desiro Classic** — explicitly *"vom Betriebskonzept bis Systemarchitektur **nach CENELEC Prozess**"*, with **sector-recognised specifications**, a **prototype RTO system for BOTH retrofit and new vehicles**, and laboratory and field validation laying **the basis for later certification and broad industrial deployment**. **⚠️ SO REMOTE TRAIN OPERATION IS NOT A RESEARCH QUESTION IN GERMANY. IT IS A €40 MILLION PROGRAMME, COORDINATED BY THE INCUMBENT SUPPLIER, WITH THE INCUMBENT OPERATOR'S FLEET AND WORKS, RUNNING NOW, BUILDING A CENELEC-PROCESS SAFETY ARCHITECTURE ON REAL TRAINS. Option (b) at ADR-002 item 8 — remote command in scope — is not a choice this engagement gets to weigh in the abstract; it is the direction the sector has already funded. The decision left to us is not WHETHER to accommodate it but on what terms.** Read together with E-2026-08-20-02, which establishes teleoperation as the designed **fallback level** for ATO: **the fallback is remote, the remote path is being industrialised, and it will arrive as a retrofit onto the same estate this register is migrating.** **(b) ⚠️ THE COUPLING ADR-002 MUST NOW WRITE DOWN, AND IT IS THE 23-JUNE FAILURE MODE WITH THE HUMAN ON THE WRONG SIDE OF IT.** If the fallback level is a human at the far end of a link, and that link rides the bearer, then **class-4 human-in-command is bearer-dependent.** A bearer failure of the 23-June class — silent, undetected, nationwide — would then remove **the advisory layer and the fallback human together**, leaving an automated estate with neither. **The register's central incident becomes qualitatively worse under remote operation, not better: in June 2026 the trains stopped safely because a human was ON BOARD to receive a written order (*Befehl*). Remove that human to a control centre and the same silence removes the recovery path as well as the supervision path.** ⚠️ **This is OUR inference and the project page asserts nothing about it — but it is exactly the question a €40 m safety architecture must answer, and it is the question this engagement is best placed to ask. It should be put at the DZSF forum on 2 September and, if not answered there, in the letter.** **(c) THE AI HALF, AND WHERE IT LANDS ON ADR-002 ITEM 6.** The project also trials **modular, AI-based obstacle detection** for **provisioning, works and depot areas**. **Note the scoping and note it approvingly: the AI is aimed at DEPOT AND WORKS movements, not at open-line safety-critical perception — a bounded operational design domain where the consequences of a miss are lower and the environment is more controlled. That is exactly the constraint ADR-002 item 6 adopted on 2026-08-20 (implementation class bound to decision class), arrived at independently and now visible as industrial practice.** The pairing is instructive: **verifiable remote-control architecture for the safety-critical path, learned perception in the bounded low-consequence domain.** **(d) RETROFIT AND CONCENTRATION.** The prototype is explicitly **for retrofit as well as new vehicles**, which places RTO inside ADR-009's retrofit population and R13's fleet dependency — **a second thing the ~16,000–21,000 vehicles may have to accept, on the same approval bottleneck STREAMLINE describes (E-2026-08-20-04d).** And **Siemens Mobility coordinating is the FOURTH place Siemens sits in this register's evidence base** (ERJU cyber · ATO-RISK · ATO-Sense · here) — see E-2026-08-20-04a. **The body that will produce the reference remote-operation architecture is the body already behind the standardisation and the national risk methodology. R8/PR13 is no longer only a supply-side concern.** **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-002 item 8 gains the sector's answer** — remote command is in scope because it is funded and under construction; **the item stays OPEN because the terms are ours to set**, specifically the bearer-availability precondition per decision class and the defined behaviour on loss of command connectivity. **ADR-004 gains** the note that a remote command path crosses the boundary differently from a local one. **ADR-009/R13 gains** RTO as a further retrofit candidate. **R3/R4 gains** the finding that loss of command connectivity is a fail-SOFT question and, under teleoperation, an existential one. **NO STATUS FLIPS — and none is warranted: a project page for a programme three years from completion is not test evidence.** R3 **Strengthened post-incident — open** · R4 **Open** · R10 **Accepted (ARB)** · R11 **Proposed — load-bearing** · ADR-002 **Accepted (ARB) — settled internally** · ADR-004/-009 **Proposed**. |

| E-2026-08-20-06 | 2026-08-20 | **FASaN — Fahrerassistenzsysteme adaptive Nachhaltigkeit im Bahnbetrieb.** DLR-Institut für Verkehrssystemtechnik with partners; client **Bundesministerium für Digitales und Verkehr (BMDV)**, **mFUND**; **project volume €2,374,808, of which 66 % BMDV funding**. Successor to the earlier **FAS-D** project. Publications named on the page incl. Meirich, Ritzer, Reiher, Ullrich, Franz (2023), *ETR* 1+2/2023 pp. 26–30, and Schnücker, Naumann, Klencke (2023) on requirements for advanced driver assistance | Funded national project — project page read at source | `https://www.dlr.de/de/ts/forschung-und-transfer/projekte/fasan`, read 2026-08-20 | **A** | **ADR-002/R10** (primary) · **ADR-004/R11** · R12 · PR4 | **validate** | **TIER A as to the project's premise, funding and scope** — the performing institute's own page. Plan-not-outcome as to results, but **the item of value here is not a result; it is the DESIGN PREMISE the project is funded on.** **(a) ⚠️ THE GUARDRAIL, IN A FUNDED GERMAN RAIL PROJECT, IN VERY NEARLY OUR OWN WORDS.** The project's opening premise, paraphrased minimally because the phrasing is the point: **driver assistance systems in rail operation can support train drivers in their work *ohne in die Fahrzeugsteuerung oder Sicherungstechnik einzugreifen* — WITHOUT INTERVENING IN VEHICLE CONTROL OR IN THE SIGNALLING/SAFETY TECHNOLOGY.** **That is ADR-002's non-negotiable — agents advise and never actuate; the certified kernel is untouched — stated as the founding constraint of a €2.37 m BMDV-funded programme. This register has argued that boundary from first principles for eight weeks; here it is as an accepted industrial design premise, independently arrived at, in domain, with public money behind it.** **(b) WHAT THE ASSISTANCE ACTUALLY DOES, AND WHY THE SHAPE MATTERS TO US.** A **networked** driver-assistance system: connectivity **between trains** lets acceleration events be de-conflicted so **load peaks are avoided**; **current predictions of passenger-exchange time** feed the driving recommendations and thereby improve **punctuality**; the improved information position is also used to **improve passenger information**. DLR's own contributions are new data sources, recommendations that avoid load peaks and account for expected passenger volumes, and improving passenger information through **co-creation processes involving all actor groups**. **⚠️ Note the architecture: the system reads a wider information picture than any single train has, and returns RECOMMENDATIONS to a human who remains in control. That is precisely ADR-002's decision plane / runtime plane arrangement — and it is precisely the "isolation gap" ADR-004 records from E-2026-08-19-01, where the safety-carrying system is deliberately cut off from timetable and delay data and only the human spans the gap. FASaN fills that gap the same way this engagement proposes to: by informing the human, not by wiring the data into the vital layer.** **(c) THE ACCEPTANCE FINDING, WHICH IS THE PART ADR-002 UNDER-WEIGHTS.** The page states plainly that **involving the train drivers is elemental to a good solution and raises acceptance of the system, which is a PRECONDITION for achieving the other goals**, and DLR's workstream includes **training and motivation concepts** to raise driver acceptance. **⚠️ ADR-002 treats automation bias as a designed-against failure and requires dissent to be cheap — but it has nothing on ACCEPTANCE as a precondition of the system working at all. This says the causal chain runs the other way from the one the register assumes: without operator acceptance the efficiency and punctuality benefits are not merely reduced, they are unreachable. Read with E-2026-08-18-08 (internal controls strengthen safety culture only where they serve improvement and shared learning rather than pure monitoring), the pattern is consistent and the register should stop treating acceptance as a soft consideration.** **NO DECISION MOVED — because it corroborates rather than establishes:** the advise-never-actuate boundary is already ADR-002's ratified non-negotiable and ADR-004's whole subject, and a project premise — however well aligned — is not evidence that the boundary is CORRECT, only that it is shared. **What it does do is strengthen the EBA/DZSF-facing argument considerably: the position is not a consultant's construction but a premise the German sector already funds.** ⚠️ **And it opens one thing that is NOT closed: acceptance as a precondition is absent from ADR-002 and is flagged here for its next read-back (due 2026-11-15) rather than bolted on today.** **NO STATUS CHANGE:** R10 **Accepted (ARB)** · R11 **Proposed — load-bearing** · R12 **Proposed — load-bearing** · ADR-002 **Accepted (ARB) — settled internally** · ADR-004 **Proposed**. |

| E-2026-08-20-07 | 2026-08-20 | **Two DZSF/SRCC projects on the APPROVAL of AI in safety-critical rail, read together.** **(i) ATO-Einsatzszenarien — *Systematisierung der Einsatzszenarien für ATO*** ("Which tests should an automated train be able to pass?"); main client **DZSF**, **DLR-TS as subcontractor to INAVET GmbH**; runtime **05/2024 – 04/2027**. **(ii) KI-Systeme — *KI-bezogene Test- und Zulassungsmethoden* / KI-Verfahren für sicherheitskritische Bahnanwendungen**; coordinator **TU Chemnitz** (chairs of Operating Systems, Media Informatics, Private Law & IP, plus the technology-transfer centre) with the **Smart Rail Connectivity Campus Annaberg-Buchholz** | Contracted-research project pages, read at source | `.../projekte/ato-einsatzszenarien` and `.../projekte/ki-systeme`, read 2026-08-20 | **A** | **ADR-010** (primary — item 5, the completeness argument) · **ADR-007** · **ADR-002** item 6 · **ADR-004/R11** · ADR-003 | **revise** | **TIER A as to scope, client, partners and dates.** ⚠️ **BOTH ARE IN FLIGHT AND NEITHER HAS PUBLISHED RESULTS — ATO-Einsatzszenarien runs to April 2027. What is logged is the SHAPE of the work and the problem statements, which are decision-relevant on their own; the outputs are not yet evidence and must be revisited.** **(a) ⚠️ THE PROBLEM STATEMENT IS OURS, WRITTEN BY THE SAFETY AUTHORITY'S RESEARCH CENTRE.** ATO-Einsatzszenarien's premise, paraphrased: at **GoA 3/4**, cameras and other sensors take over observation of the train's surroundings from the driver, and **AI will be used to process the sensor data**; this is **a challenge for the necessary approval, because the safety of the new technical systems can, IN PRINCIPLE, no longer be demonstrated by a complete analysis of how they function** (*"lässt sich prinzipbedingt nicht mehr durch eine vollständige Analyse der Funktionsweise nachweisen"*). **This is the third independent formulation of the same limit already recorded at E-2026-08-19-05 (DZSF: no analytical proof excluding errors on unknown inputs), E-2026-08-19-09 (DIN SPEC 92005: scope-compliance uncertainty) and E-2026-08-19-11 (DIN SPEC 13266: extrapolation extent not determinable). It is settled, in domain, and ADR-004's R11 separation rests on it more securely than the register has been claiming.** **(b) ⚠️ ATO-EINSATZSZENARIEN IS BUILDING THE COMPLETENESS ARGUMENT ADR-010 ITEM 5 NEEDS AND CANNOT CURRENTLY CONSTRUCT.** Its stated work packages: define **rail-specific operational design domains (ODD) for which the respective APPROVAL is to apply**, and which help bound the required ATO scenarios; fix a **derivation methodology and suitable description means for rail scenarios**, demonstrated against an example ODD; produce **software that generates TEST CASES as concrete parameterisations of scenarios**, with its application demonstrated; and — the part that matters most — **the construction of the argument for A CERTAIN COMPLETENESS of the scenarios with respect to the ODD** (*"der Aufbau der Argumentation einer gewissen Vollständigkeit der Szenarien bezüglich der ODD"*). **⚠️ READ THE HEDGE AND KEEP IT: "eine GEWISSE Vollständigkeit" — A CERTAIN completeness, not completeness. The safety authority's own research programme does not claim it can enumerate the scenario space; it claims it can construct an ARGUMENT about coverage relative to a bounded ODD. That is the honest form of the claim, it is the form ADR-010 item 5 should adopt verbatim, and it is a direct rebuke to any eval strategy that implies exhaustiveness. It also aligns with the approach transplanted from the automotive PEGASUS lineage, which the page says is being carried over to rail.** **ADR-007's undefined test surfaces gain a named route: ODD first, scenarios derived, test cases generated as parameterisations, coverage argued relative to the ODD.** **(c) KI-SYSTEME — A ROUTE TO A SAFETY CASE FOR AI, AND AN EXPLICIT ADMISSION THAT THE RULES MAY HAVE TO CHANGE.** Premise: approval of rail-technical innovations in safety-critical applications is **especially strict and especially costly because of the severity of accidents**, and many innovations in intelligent rail will use AI **either because no efficient solution strategy is possible with "conventional" methods, or because no clear technical specification for the task can be formulated.** Stated aims: produce an **Anwenderkompass** (user's compass) for the trial and approval process in rail; **identify possible ROUTES TO SAFETY DEMONSTRATION (*Sicherheitsnachweisführung*) for AI methods**; and **derive the NEEDS TO ADAPT OR REVISE THE APPLICABLE APPROVAL REGULATIONS.** **⚠️ THE SECOND CLAUSE OF THE PREMISE IS THE ONE ADR-002 ITEM 6 SHOULD NOTE: "no clear technical specification can be formulated" is a candidate JUSTIFICATION for reaching for a learned component, and it is a better one than performance. Our item-6 rule (decided 2026-08-20) permits learned components only in reversible classes; this supplies the test for when they are warranted there AT ALL — not "the model scores higher" but "the task cannot be specified". Where a task CAN be specified, the rule and this premise agree that it should be.** **And the third aim is the significant one institutionally: the research programme of the safety authority is openly examining whether the APPROVAL RULES THEMSELVES need revision for AI. ADR-003 concluded the layer is not high-risk as designed under Reg (EU) 2024/1689; that conclusion is about EU AI law and is untouched — but the NATIONAL approval regime for AI in rail is explicitly in motion, and any ADR that assumes today's Zulassung rules are stable is assuming something the regulator's own researchers are not.** **(d) A NOTE ON WHERE THIS WORK SITS.** KI-Systeme is a **TU Chemnitz / SRCC** initiative, not DZSF-commissioned — and its inclusion of **private-law and intellectual-property chairs** alongside operating systems and media informatics is unusual and worth watching: liability and IP in AI approval are questions this register has not touched at all. **MOVES: `revise`.** **ADR-010 item 5 gains** the ODD → scenarios → generated test cases → coverage-argument route, **and the "a certain completeness" hedge as the honest form of the claim**. **ADR-007 gains** the same route for its undefined surfaces. **ADR-002 item 6 gains** the "task cannot be specified" test for when a learned component is warranted at all. **ADR-004 gains** a third independent statement that complete analytical demonstration is unavailable in principle. **A watch is opened on national approval-rule revision for AI.** **NO STATUS FLIPS:** R11 **Proposed — load-bearing** · ADR-002 **Accepted (ARB) — settled internally** · ADR-003 **Accepted (ARB) — settled internally** · ADR-004/-007/-010 **Proposed**. |

Serviceeinrichtungen (§ 2 Nr. 9 AEG). **That clause is nearly a statutory description of the operational environment the oversight layer serves — the entity running predictive/event-driven train dispositions is a named NIS-2 regulatee in German law, not just a member of a broad sector.** **(d) STATUTORY ATTACK-DETECTION DUTY (§ 31 Abs. 2 BSIG n.F.):** Betreiber kritischer Anlagen must operate **Systeme zur Angriffserkennung** that "kontinuierlich und automatisch" capture and evaluate parameters from live operation, identify threats and provide for remediation, **Stand der Technik**, with a proportionality bound. **This is the German statutory footing for exactly what ADR-012 item 5 and R12/PR5 argue from first principles — independent, continuous detection is not a design preference, it is a KRITIS operator duty.** **MOVES: `revise` — ADR-012 item 6 FULLY CLOSED** (both halves: CRA recall paragraph E-2026-08-20-23e, NIS2UmsG in-force date here); item 4 gains the national reference (§ 32 BSIG n.F., joint Meldestelle, the final-report clock nuance); item 5 gains § 31 Abs. 2 as statutory grounding. **NO STATUS FLIPS — R14 stays Open on its own action items; a transposition date is a fact, not conformance evidence.** |

ADR-004's own note says item 1 "can be framed but not completed" without DIN VDE V 0831-103, whose normative content is paywalled and unfunded, and that the alternative is "inventing a severity scale we would then have to defend." **That framing is now partly overtaken: what is held is not the standard's normative tables but an authority-commissioned, published, WORKED APPLICATION of them by the method's own authors.** The residual is unchanged in kind and narrower in scope: severity tables, accident categories and barrier-dependence rules still are not held. **(c) THE RISK ANALYSIS IS CSM-COMPLIANT AND USES ALL THREE ACCEPTANCE PRINCIPLES** — code of practice, reference-system comparison, and explicit risk analysis (the limb ADR-004 identified as our position) built on DIN VDE V 0831-103; supplemented by a human-reliability analysis up to GoA 2. **(d) ⚠️ A PREMISE THE REGISTER SHOULD STOP CARRYING IMPLICITLY: ATO SAFETY FUNCTIONS APPORTION TO SIL 1–2, EXCEPTIONALLY 3 — NOT SIL 4.** Table 38 (expressly "informativ", and assuming the function is built wholly to that requirement **with no redundancy or diversity**): obstacle detection of objects on the line, passenger train / high speed / 1-yr proof test → **3×10⁻⁶/h ≈ SIL 1**; same for freight at high speed → **no quantitative requirement, i.e. Basisintegrität** (or 10⁻⁵/h ≈ SIL 1); obstacle detection of **rail vehicles** on the line, passenger train on-sight → **3×10⁻⁷/h ≈ SIL 2**; obstacle detection at **road/rail crossings** (permitted only to 160 km/h) → **10⁻⁷/h ≈ SIL 3**; **detection of persons in the track area**, medium/high speed → **3×10⁻⁷/h ≈ SIL 2**; persons in the platform track area, low speed without through-running → 10⁻⁵/h ≈ SIL 1, **with** through-running → 10⁻⁶/h ≈ SIL 2. **R11 is framed as "deterministic SIL-4 kernel outside the learning agents" — correct for the VITAL CCS kernel (interlocking/ETCS), but the perception functions a learning component would serve are apportioned SIL 1–2. The report's own conclusion: **if a technical system replacing a train driver is required to meet SIL 1 or even SIL 2, that requirement is STRICTER than the human it replaces, and is therefore conservative.** **(f) THE GoA-4 BARRIER RULE, WHICH SHARPENS HUMAN-IN-COMMAND:** the safety argument demonstrating the required integrity level **may not include the Triebfahrzeugführer as a barrier in GoA 4 operation** (involving train staff in GoA 3 may be possible). **Once the human is removed, they cannot be claimed as a mitigation — a discipline that applies equally to any oversight-layer argument that leans on "the operator would catch it."** **(g) Bounds:** SIL labels are the report's own informative gloss, not apportioned requirements; the no-redundancy/no-diversity assumption is load-bearing and rarely true in a real design; ATO-RISK expressly excludes cyber security and human performance (its conditions R4/R5), so it does not extend whole to a security-relevant, human-facing oversight layer. **MOVES: `revise` — ADR-004's §"procedure to follow" acquisition note is amended: the DIN VDE V 0831-103 purchase drops from "highest-priority acquisition, item 1 cannot be completed without it" to "still wanted for normative tables only — the worked system definition and validated outputs are now held at tier A"; and the ADR gains a grounding note carrying the SIL-1–2 apportionment, the human-reliability benchmark and the GoA-4 barrier rule. All influenced ratings — but **"the factor with the strongest impact was people's position relative to the tracks, although participants had explicitly been instructed that the AI could not process such information."** The author's conclusion: **"humans may sometimes evaluate more than the AI's performance on the assigned task"**, and **"such mismatches between AI capabilities and human expectations should be taken into consideration when conducting safety audits of AI systems."** **(b) WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT HAZARD FROM THE ONE ITEM 12 ALREADY NAMES.** Item 12 already records **anchoring** — a reviewer shown the model's finding first is influenced by it, and a system trained on its reviewers inherits their blind spots. **This is a distinct failure: CRITERION DRIFT. The adjudicator scores the AI on RISK RELEVANCE (was the person dangerously placed?) rather than on TASK CORRECTNESS (did the detector detect?), even when told the AI cannot see the risk dimension at all. A label stream built from such adjudications is not merely noisy — it is systematically mis-specified against the task the model was trained to perform.** For an oversight layer whose evaluation depends on human adjudication, that is a design constraint, not a curiosity. **(c) A SECOND, CHEAPER LESSON FOR ITEM 1:** the **elicitation method itself changed the ratings.** Any eval harness must therefore FIX and DOCUMENT how judgements are elicited, and treat a change of elicitation method as a change to the measurement instrument — not a neutral UI decision. **(d) MISSES vs FALSE ALARMS — the register should not assume the automotive ordering.** The paper summarises prior work: false alarms are often found more detrimental than misses, but that depends on task difficulty, and for EASY tasks misses and false alarms had similar impact; in rail, false alarms cause unnecessary braking while misses risk fatalities. **The asymmetry is domain- and difficulty-specific and must be measured, not inherited.** **(e) NEW POINTERS, not held:** Müller & Schmidt (2024) — collision-risk assessment "requires far more than simply detecting potential obstacles"; Gesmann-Nuissl & Kunitz (2022) and Roßbach et al. (2024) on safety-audit methods and standards for rail AI. **(f) Bounds:** laboratory participants, simulated AI, image sequences; the experiments' quantitative results were not read at this pass; no claim is made here about effect sizes. **MOVES: `revise` — ⚠️ RECORDED AS A PROPOSED AMENDMENT TO A RATIFIED ADR, NOT FOLDED IN. Bhd. is a s. 17 third party — directly bound and directly criminally liable, regardless of what the delivery contract says.** This is not a compliance detail to be handled at contracting; it is a scoping fact that belongs in the Track B charter's instrument landscape. **(d) THE PATTERN, NOW TWICE.** E-2026-08-23-03 recorded that Act 854's enforcement is **criminal, not administrative** (≤ RM 500,000 and/or ≤ 10 years) and warned Track B artifacts never to assume the German administrative posture. **Act 864 is the second Malaysian instrument in the register placing CRIMINAL liability directly on a private actor** (≤ RM 1,000,000 and/or ≤ 5 years). Where the question is "does this instrument bind us", tier C is not evidence — it is a pointer to the only thing that is.** **MOVES: `revise` — the Track B instrument landscape gains Act 864 as a MATERIAL instrument, not a de-prioritised one: s. 17 makes a private Sdn. Bhd. performing migration/integration/analytics on shared federal data a directly-bound, criminally-liable third party. E-2026-09-04-10's scoping judgement is marked superseded in place. The "criminal enforcement is the Track B default" reading is promoted from a single-instrument observation to a two-instrument working assumption. That is the same bearer-dependency this register worked at ADR-002 item 8 (remote human-in-command) and at E-2026-09-04-12 (commands over FRMCS), arriving now at the AUTHENTICATION layer: if the link drops, on-board access control runs on possibly-stale cached authorisations. ⚠️ Two consequences the document does not draw: a cache has a staleness window, and a revoked credential remains valid on-board until the cache refreshes — so credential REVOCATION is bearer-dependent in exactly the way command authority is. The **operator adds the Secure Component to the IAM**, and that IAM entry is what verifies the component is **currently allowed to commission**. Division of labour: **the supplier installs its own trust anchor and assists with the operator's; the operator installs its own, registers the component and activates commissioning; the rest is mostly automatic.** **⚠️ This is provenance enforced at first power-on rather than asserted on paper — a component that cannot present an MDC chaining to a known supplier trust anchor cannot join. It is the strongest available answer to T_020 "products from an unreliable source" (E-2026-09-05-03), and it is a mechanism, not a clause.** **(e) ⚠️ WHAT NEITHER DOCUMENT DOES: neither mentions FRMCS at all** (zero occurrences in both), and both are written for **EU-Rail Secure Components** in the CCS estate. **The mechanisms transfer as design patterns; the specifications do not cover the bearer, and no claim about FRMCS commissioning or FRMCS identity management may rest on these.** **(f) Bounds:** partial reads; the IAM document is 70 informative statements to a single recommendation, so it is a description of the EU-Rail design and not a source of obligations. **MOVES: `revise` — ADR-012's threat model gains the ON-BOARD IAM CACHE STALENESS finding (revocation is bearer-dependent) and item 2's gate gains the trust-anchor/MDC commissioning flow as the enforceable form of supply-chain provenance; ADR-004 gains a note that an oversight layer trusting on-board identity assertions inherits the cache window. This expressly includes systems that are NEWLY DELIVERED AND/OR INSTALLED** but not developed, integrated or maintained according to the relevant regulations, standards and specifications — **EULYNX BL4R2 or newer, ERJU SP Cybersecurity Requirements, CLC/TS 50701, EN IEC 62443. "Only systems developed according to the applicable and relevant regulations are treated as non-legacy."** **⚠️ The register — and ADR-011 in particular — has treated "legacy" as the OLD estate: the GSM-R installed base, the systems the migration is moving away from. On the sector's own definition, a brand-new FRMCS component procured without conformance to those specifications IS LEGACY ON THE DAY IT IS INSTALLED. That inverts the intuition behind the migration: the transition does not automatically retire the legacy problem, and can manufacture new legacy if ADR-012's procurement gate does not bind. It also gives ADR-012 item 2's gate a much sharper justification than "good practice" — the gate is what determines whether what you buy is legacy on arrival.** **(b) THE COMPENSATING-MEASURE ROUTE IS AN ESTABLISHED PROCESS, NOT AN IMPROVISATION.** 25E157 runs: check of side conditions → definition of legacy → approach → risk assessment overview → detailed risk assessment and **counter-measure evaluation**, built by first checking input documents for **available compensating counter measures**, drawing on **X2R3-WP08-T8.4 D8.2-5 "Security of legacy systems"** among others. **ADR-012 item 3 closed on 2026-09-04 with the case "where the PDE cannot take an update at all, the expedited path does not apply — that is a compensating-control decision, and must be recognised as one." Recorded as a design option with its trade-off visible, not adopted.** **(e) Bounds:** 25E157 binds nobody by its own disclaimer and expressly leaves railways full discretion in how they supervise NIS-2 compliance; 24E122's mandatory clauses bind nobody either, being EUG guidance; neither mentions FRMCS. **MOVES: `revise` — ADR-011 gains the TIME-INDEPENDENT LEGACY DEFINITION and the consequence that non-conformant new procurement creates legacy on arrival, which sharpens ADR-012 item 2's gate rationale; ADR-012 item 3's compensating-control case gains the 25E157 process as its worked route; ADR-011's pre-change gate gains the four mandatory re-measurement obligations for any VPN/security overlay on a live network. ## How to append

When something arrives during the day:
1. Add a row with the next `E-` id.
2. Set the trust tier honestly (A–D). Discount vendor superlatives; mark opinion as opinion.
3. Note which requirement(s) it touches and the action.
4. **Answer the decision question explicitly — MANDATORY, no row is complete without it (rule added 2026-08-15).** Every row must end with either:
   - **`MOVES:`** — name the decision it changes (requirement status, ADR, action item), make that edit in `traceability-matrix.md` and/or the ADR **in the same sitting**, and set the action to `revise`; or
   - **`NO DECISION MOVED — because …`** — and give the reason in one clause. "Corroborates an existing position", "below the evidence bar", "informational only", "plan not outcome" are all legitimate. **What is not legitimate is leaving the question unanswered**, because that is indistinguishable from not having asked it.
5. At end of day, run `scripts/baseline.sh` to freeze the state.

**Why rule 4 exists.** By 2026-08-15 this log held 338 rows against **0 of 9 ratified ADRs**, 55 open action items and 4 closed. Only **5%** of rows were actioned `revise`. The two founding ADRs had gone seven weeks without a read-back and had silently drifted — ADR-001 carried a switch-off date this log had itself marked superseded on day one, and ADR-002 asserted an EU AI Act high-risk posture that ADR-003 had disproved the same day it was written. Both defects were **visible in the evidence log the whole time**; nothing forced anyone to look. Written up in `linkedin-post-decision-drift.md`; repaired 2026-08-15.

**The health metric.** `scripts/baseline.sh` now emits a decision-health block in every `BASELINE.md`: ADRs by status, action items open vs closed, and the **revise rate**. **Watch the revise rate.** If it sits near 5% while intake continues, the wire between evidence and decisions is disconnected — however good the log looks. A high `validate` share is not a sign of health; it is the signature of a register confirming what it already believed.

Gates R11 / ADR-004; ADR-003's "not high-risk" leans on unlicensed EN 50129 composition wording → carried as an ASSUMPTION. **Narrowed 2026-07-31/2026-08-01 (E-2026-07-31-05, E-2026-08-01-01):** both EN 50128:2011 amendments now on file PRIMARY — A1:2020 (Annex ZZ: harmonisation/presumption-of-conformity vs Dir 2016/797 + CCS TSI) and A2:2020 (alignment with EN 50126-1/-2:2017 + EN 50129:2018; Basic Integrity replaces SIL 0; IT-security delegated to IEC 62443; A2 preview TRUNCATED — sections 11–17 unread). The technical CLAUSE BODIES of EN 50128:2011 (and EN 50126/50129/50159) remain paywalled → residual stands. **Successor CONFIRMED 2026-08-01 (E-2026-08-01-10, primary):** EN 50716:2023 supersedes EN 50128:2011 (+AC:2014, A1, A2) AND EN 50657:2017 — the residual's full-text purchase target is now EN 50716:2023, NOT EN 50128. **TSI-edition RESOLVED same day (E-2026-08-01-11, EU law), REFINED to a three-layer rule (E-2026-08-01-13):** (1) edition BY REGIME — base 2023/1695 Table A 3 cites EN 50128:2011 (pre-amendment regimes, Appendix B), the 2026/693-amended Table A 3 cites EN 50716:2023 (Note 3 grandfathers EN 50128); (2) Table A 3 is a NON-EXCLUSIVE SAFE HARBOUR into CSM-RA — alternatives with proven equivalence permitted; (3) the Art.17/2016/797 PRESUMPTION runs through EN 50716 only (CID 2025/424 row 114a, since 2025-03-06; 2016/919-scoped per recital 5); EN 50128's presumption has LAPSED (absent from the current harmonised list). - **GSMA FS.11 (SS7) / FS.19 (Diameter) / FS.20 (GTP) interconnect-security guidelines — MEMBER-ONLY, accepted residual (recorded 2026-08-01).** Unlike the purchasable CENELEC/IEC texts, these are membership-gated. **Narrowed by the public set on file** (FS.57 MoTIF E-2026-08-01-04 · FS.61 micro-segmentation -07 · FS.56 MDSCert -08 · FS.40 5G Security Guide -09): GSMA's architecture guidance, assurance schemes (NESAS/SCAS, FS.40 §18), legacy-coexistence risks (FS.40 §12) and interconnect border functions (IPUPS, FS.40 §11) are all publicly documented — what stays gated is the detailed operational hardening parameters. **The gating is itself evidence for the §4a gap:** the operational interconnect-security knowledge for the technology FRMCS adopts lives inside a membership club rail doesn't belong to — the ETSI-TC-RT-for-GSMA substitution transfers the architecture role, not the membership benefits. **Verify-watch:** is DB InfraGO (or any FRMCS operator / ERA / UIC) a GSMA member or T-ISAC participant? National-roaming MNO partners (INB 2026, E-2026-07-28-01) have full access — a possible contractual channel.
